translations.idiomatic: Zizhi Tongjian, Volume 281.

sentences.zh: 【後晉紀二】 起強圉作噩，盡著雍閹茂，凡二年。

translations.literal: [Later Jin Annals 2] From Qiangyu Zuo'e through Zhuyong Xianmao; two years in all.
translations.idiomatic: [Later Jin Annals 2] From Qiangyu Zuo'e through Zhuyong Xianmao—two years in all.

sentences.zh: 高祖聖文章武明德孝皇帝上之下天福二年（

translations.literal: Gaozu the Sagely Literary Martial Virtuous Filial Emperor, Part Two Below, Tianfu year 2 (
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu the Sagely Literary Martial Virtuous Filial Emperor, Part Two Below—Tianfu year 2 (

sentences.zh: 丁酉，公元九三七年）

translations.literal: dingyou, AD 937)
translations.idiomatic: dingyou, AD 937)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，乙卯，日有食之。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on yimao, there was an eclipse of the sun.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on the day yimao, the sun was eclipsed.

sentences.zh: 詔以前北面招收指揮使安重榮為成德節度使，以秘瓊為齊州防禦使。

translations.literal: An edict appointed the former Northern Face recruitment and receipt commander An Chongrong as Chengde military governor, and Mi Qiong as Qizhou defense commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: The court appointed An Chongrong, former commander of the Northern Face recruitment forces, military governor of Chengde, and made Mi Qiong defense commissioner of Qizhou.

sentences.zh: 遣引進使王景崇諭瓊以利害。

translations.literal: The court sent the reception commissioner Wang Jingchong to explain the advantages and disadvantages to Qiong.
translations.idiomatic: It dispatched Reception Commissioner Wang Jingchong to lay out the stakes for Qiong.

sentences.zh: 重榮與契丹將趙思溫偕如鎮州，瓊不敢拒命。

translations.literal: Chongrong went to Zhenzhou together with the Khitan general Zhao Siwen; Qiong did not dare refuse the order.
translations.idiomatic: Chongrong traveled to Zhenzhou alongside the Khitan general Zhao Siwen, and Qiong dared not defy the appointment.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，重榮奏已視事。

translations.literal: On bingchen, Chongrong memorialized that he had already assumed office.
translations.idiomatic: On bingchen, Chongrong reported that he had taken up his post.

sentences.zh: 景崇，邢州人也。

translations.literal: Jingchong was a native of Xingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Jingchong came from Xingzhou.

sentences.zh: 契丹以幽州為南京。

translations.literal: The Khitan made Youzhou their Southern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan designated Youzhou as their Southern Capital.

sentences.zh: 李崧、呂琦逃匿於伊闕民間。

translations.literal: Li Song and Lü Qi hid themselves among the common people of Yique.
translations.idiomatic: Li Song and Lü Qi went into hiding among the common people of Yique.

sentences.zh: 帝以始鎮河東，崧有力焉，德之；

translations.literal: Because when the emperor first held Hedong, Song had rendered him great service, he was grateful to him;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor remembered that Song had helped him greatly when he first secured Hedong, and he held him in esteem;

sentences.zh: 亦不責琦。

translations.literal: he also did not blame Qi.
translations.idiomatic: nor did he blame Qi.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，以琦為秘書監；

translations.literal: On yichou, Qi was made director of the Secretariat;
translations.idiomatic: On yichou, Qi was appointed director of the Secretariat;

sentences.zh: 丙寅，以崧為兵部侍郎、判戶部。

translations.literal: on bingyin, Song was made vice minister of war and overseer of the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: on bingyin, Song was made vice minister of war with concurrent charge of the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 初，天雄節度使兼中書令范延光微時，有術士張生語之云：「必為將相。」

translations.literal: Earlier, when Fan Yanguang, military governor of Tianxiong and concurrent chief councilor, was still obscure, a diviner named Zhang told him, "You are certain to become a general or minister."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Fan Yanguang—later military governor of Tianxiong and chief councilor—was still obscure, a diviner named Zhang told him, "You are destined for high command and high office."

sentences.zh: 延光既貴，信重之。

translations.literal: After Yanguang rose to eminence, he trusted and valued him greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Once Yanguang had risen to power, he trusted Zhang implicitly.

sentences.zh: 延光嘗夢蛇自臍入腹，以問張生，張生曰：「蛇者龍也，帝王之兆。」

translations.literal: Yanguang once dreamed that a serpent entered his belly through the navel; he asked Zhang about it, and Zhang said, "A serpent is a dragon—an omen of imperial rule."
translations.idiomatic: Yanguang once dreamed of a serpent entering his belly through the navel. When he asked Zhang about it, Zhang said, "A serpent is a dragon in disguise—an omen of kingship."

sentences.zh: 延光由是有非望之志。

translations.literal: From this Yanguang harbored ambitions beyond his station.
translations.idiomatic: From that dream Yanguang began to nurse ambitions beyond his station.

sentences.zh: 唐潞王素與延光善，及趙德鈞敗，延光自遼州引兵還魏州，雖奉表請降，內不自安，以書潛結秘瓊，欲與之為亂。

translations.literal: The Tang Prince of Lu had always been on good terms with Yanguang; when Zhao Dejun was defeated, Yanguang led his troops back from Liaozhou to Weizhou; though he submitted a memorial requesting surrender, inwardly he was uneasy, and by secret letter he tried to win Mi Qiong to join him in rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: The Tang Prince of Lu had long been friendly with Yanguang. After Zhao Dejun's defeat, Yanguang withdrew from Liaozhou to Weizhou. Though he formally submitted and asked to surrender, he was uneasy at heart and secretly wrote to Mi Qiong, hoping to draw him into a revolt.

sentences.zh: 瓊受其書不報，延光恨之。

translations.literal: Qiong received his letter but did not reply; Yanguang resented him for it.
translations.idiomatic: Qiong received the letter but never answered, and Yanguang came to hate him.

sentences.zh: 瓊將之齊，過魏境，延光欲滅口，且利其貨，遣兵邀之於夏津，殺之。

translations.literal: When Qiong was about to go to Qi, he passed through Wei's territory; Yanguang wished to silence him and also coveted his goods, so he sent troops to intercept him at Xiajin and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: As Qiong was setting out for Qi, his route took him through Wei's territory. Yanguang wanted him dead both to silence him and to seize his goods, so he sent troops to ambush him at Xiajin and killed him.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，延光奏稱夏津捕盜兵誤殺瓊；

translations.literal: On dingmao, Yanguang memorialized that troops hunting bandits at Xiajin had mistakenly killed Qiong;
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao, Yanguang reported that troops hunting bandits at Xiajin had killed Qiong by mistake;

sentences.zh: 帝不問。

translations.literal: the emperor did not pursue the matter.
translations.idiomatic: the emperor let the matter drop.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，以李崧為中書侍郎、同平章事，充樞密使，桑維翰兼樞密使。

translations.literal: On wuyin, Li Song was made vice director of the Secretariat, associate chief councilor, and full privy councilor; Sang Weihan was made concurrent privy councilor.
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin, Li Song was appointed vice director of the Secretariat, associate chief councilor, and chief privy councilor, while Sang Weihan received a concurrent appointment as privy councilor.

sentences.zh: 時晉新得天下，籓鎮多未服從；

translations.literal: At this time Jin had only recently won the realm, and many military governors had not yet submitted;
translations.idiomatic: Jin had only lately taken the realm, and many military governors had yet to submit;

sentences.zh: 或雖服從，反仄不安。

translations.literal: or even if they had submitted, they were restless and uneasy.
translations.idiomatic: while even those who had submitted remained restless and uneasy.

sentences.zh: 兵火之餘，府庫殫竭，民間困窮，而契丹徵求無厭。

translations.literal: After the fires of war, the treasuries were exhausted, the people were destitute, and yet the Khitan demands were insatiable.
translations.idiomatic: The fires of war had emptied the treasuries and left the people in want, even as Khitan exactions knew no end.

sentences.zh: 維翰勸帝推誠棄怨以撫籓鎮，卑辭厚禮以奉契丹，訓卒繕兵以修武備，務農桑以實倉廩，通商賈以豐貨財。

translations.literal: Weihan urged the emperor to win over the military governors by showing sincerity and laying aside grievances, to honor the Khitan with humble words and rich gifts, to drill troops and repair arms to strengthen defenses, to promote farming and sericulture to fill the granaries, and to encourage merchants to enrich the state's wealth.
translations.idiomatic: Weihan urged the emperor to win the military governors with sincerity and by laying old grievances aside, to placate the Khitan with humble words and lavish gifts, to drill the army and repair arms, to promote farming and sericulture so the granaries would fill again, and to encourage trade so wealth would return.

sentences.zh: 數年之間，中國稍安。

translations.literal: Within a few years, the Central Realm grew somewhat settled.
translations.idiomatic: Within a few years the heartland grew somewhat calm again.

sentences.zh: 吳太子璉納齊王知誥女為妃。

translations.literal: The Wu crown prince Bian took the daughter of the Prince of Qi, Zhigao, as consort.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Crown Prince Bian married a daughter of Prince of Qi Zhigao.

sentences.zh: 知誥始建太廟、社稷，改金陵為江寧府，牙城曰宮城，廳堂曰殿；

translations.literal: Zhigao first established the Grand Ancestral Temple and the altars of soil and grain, changed Jinling to Jiangning Prefecture, called the barracks city the palace city and the main halls palaces;
translations.idiomatic: Zhigao founded the Grand Ancestral Temple and the altars of soil and grain, renamed Jinling Jiangning Prefecture, styled the barracks city a palace city and its main halls palaces;

sentences.zh: 以左、右司馬宋齊丘、徐玠為左、右丞相，馬步判官周宗、內樞判官黟人周廷玉為內樞使。

translations.literal: he made the left and right marshals Song Qiuqiu and Xu Jie left and right chief ministers, the cavalry and infantry judge Zhou Zong and the inner-pivot judge Zhou Tingyu of Yi county inner-pivot commissioners.
translations.idiomatic: he appointed marshals Song Qiuqiu and Xu Jie left and right chief ministers, and made cavalry-and-infantry judge Zhou Zong and inner-pivot judge Zhou Tingyu of Yi county inner-pivot commissioners.

sentences.zh: 自餘百官皆如吳朝之制。

translations.literal: All other officials followed the Wu court's institutions.
translations.idiomatic: All other offices followed Wu court precedent.

sentences.zh: 置騎兵八軍，步兵九軍。

translations.literal: He established eight cavalry armies and nine infantry armies.
translations.idiomatic: He organized eight cavalry armies and nine infantry armies.

sentences.zh: 二月，吳主以盧文進為宣武節度使，兼侍中。

translations.literal: In the second month, the Wu ruler made Lu Wenjin military governor of Xuanwu and concurrent palace attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, the Wu ruler appointed Lu Wenjin military governor of Xuanwu with the concurrent title of palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 戊子，吳主使宜陽王璪如西都，冊命齊王；

translations.literal: On wuzi, the Wu ruler sent Prince Yiyang Bian to the Western Capital to invest the Prince of Qi;
translations.idiomatic: On wuzi, the Wu ruler sent Prince Yiyang Bian to the Western Capital to invest the Prince of Qi;

sentences.zh: 王受冊，赦境內。

translations.literal: the prince received the investiture and proclaimed an amnesty within his domain.
translations.idiomatic: the prince accepted the investiture and proclaimed an amnesty throughout his domain.

sentences.zh: 冊王妃曰王后。

translations.literal: His consort was invested as queen.
translations.idiomatic: His consort was invested as queen.

sentences.zh: 吳越王元瓘之弟順化節度使、同平章事元珦獲罪於元瓘，廢為庶人。

translations.literal: Yuan Xun, younger brother of the King of Wuyue Yuan Qian, military governor of Shunhua and associate chief councilor, offended Yuan Qian and was degraded to commoner status.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Xun, younger brother of Wuyue King Yuan Qian and military governor of Shunhua with the title of associate chief councilor, fell foul of Yuan Qian and was reduced to commoner status.

sentences.zh: 契丹主自上黨歸，過雲州，大同節度使沙彥珣出迎，契丹主留之，不使還鎮。

translations.literal: The Khitan ruler returned from Shangdang and passed through Yunzhou; Datong military governor Sha Yanxun came out to welcome him, but the Khitan ruler detained him and would not let him return to his post.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan ruler was returning from Shangdang when he passed Yunzhou. Datong military governor Sha Yanxun came out to welcome him, but the Khitan ruler detained him and would not let him return to his command.

sentences.zh: 節度判官吳巒在城中，謂其眾曰：「吾屬禮義之俗，安可臣於夷狄乎！」

translations.literal: The military governor's aide Wu Luan was in the city and said to the troops, "We belong to a land of ritual and righteousness—how can we submit to barbarians!"
translations.idiomatic: Military governor's aide Wu Luan was still in the city. He told the troops, "We are people of ritual and righteousness—how can we bow to barbarians!"

sentences.zh: 眾推巒領州事，閉城不受契丹之命，契丹攻之，不克。

translations.literal: The men urged Luan to take charge of the prefecture, closed the gates and refused Khitan orders; the Khitan attacked but could not take it.
translations.idiomatic: The troops pressed Luan to take charge of the prefecture. They shut the gates, refused Khitan orders, and when the Khitan attacked they could not take the city.

sentences.zh: 應州馬軍都指揮使金城郭崇威亦恥臣契丹，挺身南歸。

translations.literal: Guo Chongwei of Jincheng, cavalry commander of Yingzhou, likewise ashamed to serve the Khitan, made his way south alone.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Chongwei of Jincheng, cavalry commander at Yingzhou, was likewise ashamed to serve the Khitan and made his way south on his own.

sentences.zh: 契丹主過新州，命威塞節度使翟璋斂犒軍錢十萬緡。

translations.literal: When the Khitan ruler passed Xinzhou, he ordered Weisai military governor Zhai Zhang to collect one hundred thousand strings in cash to reward the army.
translations.idiomatic: Passing Xinzhou, the Khitan ruler ordered Weisai military governor Zhai Zhang to levy one hundred thousand strings in cash to reward his troops.

sentences.zh: 初，契丹主阿保機強盛，室韋、奚、霫皆役屬焉，奚王去諸苦契丹貪虐，帥其眾西徙媯州，依劉仁恭父子，號西奚。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the Khitan ruler Abaoji grew powerful, the Shiwei, Xi, and Mohe all became his subjects; the Xi king Quzhu, suffering from Khitan greed and cruelty, led his people west to Gui Prefecture to rely on Liu Rengong and his sons, and was called the Western Xi.
translations.idiomatic: In earlier days, when Khitan ruler Abaoji grew powerful, the Shiwei, Xi, and Mohe all fell under his sway. Xi king Quzhu, weary of Khitan greed and cruelty, led his people west to Gui Prefecture to shelter under Liu Rengong and his sons, and they came to be called the Western Xi.

sentences.zh: 去諸卒，子掃刺立。

translations.literal: When Quzhu died, his son Saoci succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: When Quzhu died, his son Saoci succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 唐莊宗滅劉守光，賜掃刺姓李名紹威。

translations.literal: When Tang's Emperor Zhuangzong destroyed Liu Shouguang, he granted Saoci the surname Li and the name Shaowei.
translations.idiomatic: After Tang Emperor Zhuangzong destroyed Liu Shouguang, he granted Saoci the surname Li and the name Shaowei.

sentences.zh: 紹威娶契丹逐不魯之姊。

translations.literal: Shaowei married the elder sister of the Khitan Zhubulu.
translations.idiomatic: Shaowei married the elder sister of the Khitan Zhubulu.

sentences.zh: 逐不魯獲罪於契丹，奔紹威，紹威納之；

translations.literal: Zhubulu offended the Khitan and fled to Shaowei, who took him in;
translations.idiomatic: Zhubulu fell out with the Khitan and fled to Shaowei, who gave him refuge;

sentences.zh: 契丹怒，攻之，不克。

translations.literal: the Khitan were enraged and attacked but could not prevail.
translations.idiomatic: the Khitan attacked in anger but could not prevail.

sentences.zh: 紹威卒，子拽剌立。

translations.literal: When Shaowei died, his son Zhuaici succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: When Shaowei died, his son Zhuaici succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 及契丹主德光自上黨北還，拽剌迎降，時逐不魯亦卒，契丹主曰：「汝誠無罪，掃剌、逐不魯負我。」

translations.literal: When the Khitan ruler Deguang returned north from Shangdang, Zhuaici came out to surrender; Zhubulu had also died by then, and the Khitan ruler said, "You are truly without guilt; it was Saoci and Zhubulu who wronged me."
translations.idiomatic: When Khitan ruler Deguang was returning north from Shangdang, Zhuaici came out to surrender. Zhubulu had died by then as well. The Khitan ruler said, "You are innocent; it was Saoci and Zhubulu who wronged me."

sentences.zh: 皆命發其骨，磑而揚之。

translations.literal: He ordered both men's bones exhumed, ground to powder, and scattered to the winds.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered both men's bones dug up, ground to powder, and scattered to the winds.

sentences.zh: 諸奚畏契丹之虐，多逃叛。

translations.literal: The various Xi, fearing Khitan cruelty, fled or rebelled in large numbers.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing Khitan cruelty, many Xi bands fled or rebelled.

sentences.zh: 契丹主勞翟璋曰：「當為汝除代，令汝南歸。」

translations.literal: The Khitan ruler comforted Zhai Zhang, saying, "I shall clear Dai for you and let you return south."
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan ruler reassured Zhai Zhang: "I will clear Dai for you and send you home to the south."

sentences.zh: 己亥，璋表乞征詣闕。

translations.literal: On jihai, Zhang memorialized requesting permission to come to court.
translations.idiomatic: On jihai, Zhang memorialized asking leave to come to court.

sentences.zh: 既而契丹遣璋將兵討叛奚、攻雲州，有功，留不遣璋，璋鬱鬱而卒。

translations.literal: Soon afterward the Khitan sent Zhang with troops to suppress rebellious Xi and attack Yunzhou; he achieved merit, but they kept him and would not release him, and Zhang died in dejection.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward the Khitan sent Zhang to suppress rebellious Xi and attack Yunzhou. He performed well, but they kept him from returning and he died in dejection.

sentences.zh: 張礪自契丹逃歸，為追騎所獲，契丹主責之曰：「何故捨我去？」

translations.literal: Zhang Li fled from the Khitan to return home but was caught by pursuing horsemen; the Khitan ruler rebuked him, saying, "Why did you abandon me?"
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Li fled the Khitan to return home but was caught by pursuing horsemen. The Khitan ruler rebuked him: "Why did you leave me?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「臣華人，飲食衣服皆不與此同，生不如死，願早就戮。」

translations.literal: He replied, "Your servant is a Chinese; food, drink, and clothing here are all unlike ours—life is worse than death. I beg to be executed soon."
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "I am a Chinese. Food, drink, and clothing here are nothing like ours—life is worse than death. I beg you to kill me quickly."

sentences.zh: 契丹主顧通事高彥英曰：「吾常戒汝善遇此人，何故使之失所而亡去？

translations.literal: The Khitan ruler turned to the interpreter Gao Yanying and said, "I have often warned you to treat this man well—why did you let him lose his place and flee?
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan ruler turned to interpreter Gao Yanying. "I have often told you to treat this man well—why did you let him lose his footing and run away?

sentences.zh: 若失之，安可復得邪！」

translations.literal: Once lost, how can he be recovered!"
translations.idiomatic: Once you lose a man like that, how can you get him back!"

sentences.zh: 笞彥英而謝礪。

translations.literal: He had Yanying flogged and apologized to Li.
translations.idiomatic: He had Yanying flogged and apologized to Li.

sentences.zh: 礪事契丹主甚忠直，遇事輒言，無所隱避，契丹主甚重之。

translations.literal: Li served the Khitan ruler with great loyalty and frankness, speaking out on every matter without concealment, and the Khitan ruler valued him highly.
translations.idiomatic: Li served the Khitan ruler with blunt loyalty, speaking his mind on every matter without holding back, and the Khitan ruler held him in high regard.

sentences.zh: 初，吳越王鏐少子元㺷數有軍功，鏐賜之兵仗。

translations.literal: Earlier, Qian Liu's youngest son Yuan Huang had won many military honors, and Liu bestowed arms upon him.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Qian Liu's youngest son Yuan Huang had won distinction in battle, and Liu had bestowed arms upon him.

sentences.zh: 及吳越王元瓘立，元珪為土客馬步軍都指揮使、靜江節度使，兼中書令，恃恩驕橫，增置兵仗至數千，國人多附之。

translations.literal: When the King of Wuyue Yuan Qian succeeded, Yuan Gui became commander of native and guest cavalry and infantry and military governor of Jingjiang, with concurrent chief councilor rank; relying on favor he grew arrogant, increased his arms to several thousand, and many in the state attached themselves to him.
translations.idiomatic: When Wuyue King Yuan Qian succeeded, Yuan Gui became commander of native and guest forces and military governor of Jingjiang with the concurrent title of chief councilor. Relying on imperial favor, he grew arrogant, built his arsenal to several thousand weapons, and many in the kingdom rallied to him.

sentences.zh: 元瓘忌之，使人諷元珪請輸兵仗，出判溫州，元珪不從。

translations.literal: Yuan Qian resented this and sent men to hint that Gui should turn in his arms and take assignment at Wenzhou; Gui refused.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Qian grew wary of him and sent envoys to suggest that Gui surrender his arms and take a posting at Wenzhou. Gui refused.

sentences.zh: 銅官廟吏告元瓘遣親信禱神，求主吳越江山；

translations.literal: A clerk at the Tongguan Temple reported that Yuan Qian had sent trusted men to pray to the gods to gain rule over Wuyue's lands and rivers;
translations.idiomatic: A clerk at the Tongguan Temple reported that Yuan Qian had sent trusted men to pray for rule over all Wuyue;

sentences.zh: 又為蠟丸從水竇出入，與兄元珦謀議。

translations.literal: and that wax pellets were passed in and out through a water conduit to plot with his elder brother Yuan Xun.
translations.idiomatic: and that wax pellets were passed through a water conduit to plot with his elder brother Yuan Xun.

sentences.zh: 三月，戊午，元瓘遣使者召元㺷宴宮中，既至，左右稱元珪有刃墜於懷袖，即格殺之；

translations.literal: In the third month, on wuwu, Yuan Qian sent envoys to summon Yuan Huang to a feast in the palace; once he arrived, attendants claimed a blade had fallen from Gui's sleeve, and he was killed on the spot;
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on wuwu, Yuan Qian summoned Yuan Huang to a palace feast. Once he arrived, attendants claimed a blade had fallen from Gui's sleeve, and he was killed on the spot;

sentences.zh: 並殺元珦。

translations.literal: Yuan Xun was killed as well.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Xun was killed as well.

sentences.zh: 元瓘欲按諸將吏與元珦、元珪交通者，其子仁俊諫曰：「昔光武克王郎，曹公破袁紹，皆焚其書疏以安反側，今宜效之。」

translations.literal: Yuan Qian wished to investigate all generals and officials who had dealings with Yuan Xun and Yuan Gui; his son Renjun remonstrated, saying, "In the past, when Emperor Guangwu overcame Wang Lang and Lord Cao defeated Yuan Shao, each burned the letters and documents to reassure the wavering—today we should do the same."
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Qian wanted to investigate every general and official who had dealt with Yuan Xun and Yuan Gui. His son Renjun remonstrated: "When Emperor Guangwu overcame Wang Lang and Lord Cao defeated Yuan Shao, each burned the correspondence to reassure the wavering. We should do the same."

sentences.zh: 元瓘從之。

translations.literal: Yuan Qian followed his advice.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Qian took his advice.

sentences.zh: 或得唐潞王膂及髀骨獻之，庚申，詔以王禮葬於徽陵南。

translations.literal: Someone obtained and presented the upper arm and thigh bones of the Tang Prince of Lu; on gengshen, an edict ordered them buried south of Huiling with princely rites.
translations.idiomatic: Someone presented the upper arm and thigh bones of the Tang Prince of Lu. On gengshen, an edict ordered them buried south of Huiling with princely honors.

sentences.zh: 帝遣使詣蜀告即位，且敘姻好；

translations.literal: The emperor sent envoys to Shu to announce his accession and also to renew ties of marriage alliance;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent envoys to Shu to announce his accession and renew marriage ties;

sentences.zh: 蜀主復書，用敵國禮。

translations.literal: the Shu ruler replied with the forms due between equal states.
translations.idiomatic: the Shu ruler replied in the forms due between equal states.

sentences.zh: 范延光聚卒繕兵，悉召巡內刺史集魏州，將作亂。

translations.literal: Fan Yanguang gathered troops and repaired arms, summoned all inspectors within his circuit to assemble at Weizhou, and was about to rebel.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Yanguang gathered troops, repaired arms, summoned every inspector in his circuit to Weizhou, and was preparing to rebel.

sentences.zh: 會帝謀徙都大梁，桑維翰曰：「大梁北控燕、趙，南通江、淮，水陸都會，資用富饒。

translations.literal: Just then the emperor was planning to move the capital to Daliang; Sang Weihan said, "Daliang controls Yan and Zhao to the north and connects with the Yangzi and Huai to the south—it is a meeting place by land and water, rich in resources.
translations.idiomatic: Just then the emperor was planning to move the capital to Daliang. Sang Weihan said, "Daliang commands Yan and Zhao to the north and opens on the Yangzi and Huai to the south. It is a hub by land and water, rich in supplies.

sentences.zh: 今延光反形已露，大梁距魏不過十驛，彼若有變，大軍尋至，所謂疾雷不及掩耳也。」

translations.literal: Now Yanguang's rebellious intent is already plain; Daliang is no more than ten post-stages from Wei—if trouble arises there, a great army can arrive at once, as the saying goes, 'thunderbolts give no time to cover the ears.'"
translations.idiomatic: Yanguang's rebellion is already plain. Daliang lies only ten post-stages from Wei—if he moves, a great army can be there in no time. As the saying goes, thunder gives no time to cover the ears."

sentences.zh: 丙寅，下詔，托以洛陽漕運有闕，東巡汴州。

translations.literal: On bingyin, an edict was issued, citing shortfalls in Luoyang's transport of tribute grain, to make an eastern tour to Bianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On bingyin, the court issued an edict citing shortfalls in Luoyang's grain transport and announcing an eastern tour to Bianzhou.

sentences.zh: 吳徐知誥立子景通為王太子，固辭不受。

translations.literal: Xu Zhigao of Wu installed his son Jingtong as royal heir apparent; the son firmly declined and would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Zhigao of Wu named his son Jingtong royal heir apparent, but the son firmly declined.

sentences.zh: 追尊考忠武王溫曰太祖武王，妣明德太妃李氏曰王太后。

translations.literal: He posthumously honored his father, Loyal Martial King Wen, as Grand Ancestor Martial King, and his mother, the Virtuous and Bright Grand Consort Lady Li, as royal empress dowager.
translations.idiomatic: He posthumously honored his father Loyal Martial King Wen as Grand Ancestor Martial King and his mother Virtuous and Bright Grand Consort Lady Li as royal empress dowager.

sentences.zh: 壬申，更名誥。

translations.literal: On renshen, he changed his name to Gao.
translations.idiomatic: On renshen, he changed his personal name to Gao.

sentences.zh: 庚辰，帝發洛陽，留前朔方節度使張從賓為東都巡檢使。

translations.literal: On gengchen, the emperor departed Luoyang, leaving former Shuofang military governor Zhang Congbin as eastern capital inspection commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: On gengchen, the emperor left Luoyang and left former Shuofang military governor Zhang Congbin as eastern capital inspection commissioner.

sentences.zh: 漢主以疾愈，大赦。

translations.literal: The Han ruler, his illness having abated, proclaimed a general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: The Han ruler, recovered from illness, proclaimed a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 交州將皎公羨殺安南節度使楊廷藝而代之。

translations.literal: The Jiaozhou general Jiao Gongxian killed Annan military governor Yang Tingyi and replaced him.
translations.idiomatic: The Jiaozhou general Jiao Gongxian killed Annan military governor Yang Tingyi and took his place.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，丙戌，帝至汴州；

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on bingxu, the emperor reached Bianzhou;
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on bingxu, the emperor reached Bianzhou;

sentences.zh: 丁亥，大赦。

translations.literal: on dinghai, a general amnesty was proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: on dinghai, he proclaimed a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 吳越王元瓘復建國，如同光故事。

translations.literal: The King of Wuyue Yuan Qian restored his state, following the precedent of the Tongguang era.
translations.idiomatic: Wuyue King Yuan Qian restored his kingdom on the Tongguang precedent.

sentences.zh: 丙申，赦境內，立其子弘僔為世子。

translations.literal: On bingshen, he proclaimed an amnesty within his domain and installed his son Hongpu as heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: On bingshen, he proclaimed an amnesty throughout his domain and named his son Hongpu heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 以曹仲達、沈崧、皮光業為丞相，鎮海節度判官林鼎掌教令。

translations.literal: He made Cao Zhongda, Shen Song, and Pi Guangye chief ministers, and Zhenhai military governor's aide Lin Ding overseer of edicts and orders.
translations.idiomatic: He appointed Cao Zhongda, Shen Song, and Pi Guangye chief ministers, and made Zhenhai military governor's aide Lin Ding overseer of edicts and orders.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，加宣武節度使楊光遠兼侍中。

translations.literal: On dingyou, Xuanwu military governor Yang Guangyuan was given the additional title of palace attendant.
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou, Xuanwu military governor Yang Guangyuan was given the concurrent title of palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 閩主作紫微宮，飾以水晶，土木之盛倍於寶皇宮。

translations.literal: The Min ruler built the Purple Forbidden Palace, adorned with crystal; its timber and earthworks exceeded those of the Precious Imperial Palace twofold.
translations.idiomatic: The Min ruler built the Purple Forbidden Palace, adorned with crystal, and its timber-and-earthworks surpassed the Precious Imperial Palace twofold.

sentences.zh: 又遣使散詣諸州，伺人隱慝。

translations.literal: He also sent envoys out to the various prefectures to spy on people's hidden faults.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent agents throughout the prefectures to ferret out hidden wrongdoing.

sentences.zh: 五月，吳徐誥用宋齊丘策，欲結契丹以取中國，遣使以美女、珍玩泛海修好，契丹主亦遣使報之。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, Xu Gao of Wu, using Song Qiuqiu's plan, wished to ally with the Khitan to seize the Central Realm; he sent envoys with beautiful women and rare treasures across the sea to establish friendly relations, and the Khitan ruler also sent envoys in reply.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, Xu Gao of Wu, following Song Qiuqiu's counsel, sought an alliance with the Khitan to seize the Central Realm. He sent envoys across the sea with beautiful women and rare treasures to open friendly relations, and the Khitan ruler sent envoys in reply.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，敕權署汴州牙城曰大寧宮。

translations.literal: On bingchen, an edict provisionally styled the Bianzhou barracks city the Great Tranquility Palace.
translations.idiomatic: On bingchen, an edict provisionally styled the Bianzhou barracks city the Great Tranquility Palace.

sentences.zh: 壬申，進范延光爵臨清郡王，以安其意。

translations.literal: On renshen, Fan Yanguang was advanced in rank to Prince of Linqing Commandery to reassure him.
translations.idiomatic: On renshen, Fan Yanguang was raised to Prince of Linqing Commandery to reassure him.

sentences.zh: 追尊四代考妣為帝后。

translations.literal: The four preceding generations of forebears were posthumously honored as emperor and empress.
translations.idiomatic: Four generations of forebears were posthumously honored as emperor and empress.

sentences.zh: 己卯，詔太社所藏唐室罪人首聽親舊收葬。

translations.literal: On jimao, an edict allowed kin and friends to retrieve and bury the heads of Tang criminals kept in the Grand Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: On jimao, an edict allowed kin and friends to retrieve and bury the heads of Tang criminals kept in the Grand Ancestral Temple.

sentences.zh: 初，武衛上將軍婁繼英嘗事梁均王，為內諸司使，至是，請其首而葬之。

translations.literal: Earlier, Guard General of the Right Wuwei Lou Jiying had once served Prince Jun of Liang as director of the inner bureaus; at this time he requested the prince's head and buried it.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Lou Jiying, Guard General of the Right Wuwei, had once served Prince Jun of Liang as director of the inner bureaus; now he asked for the prince's head and gave it burial.

sentences.zh: 六月，吳諸道副都統徐景遷卒。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, Xu Jingqian, deputy overall commander of all Wu circuits, died.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, Xu Jingqian, deputy overall commander of all Wu circuits, died.

sentences.zh: 范延光素以軍府之政委元隨左都押牙孫銳，銳恃恩專橫，符奏有不如意者，對延光手裂之。

translations.literal: Fan Yanguang had long delegated the military commission's affairs to Yuan Sui, left chief adjutant, and Sun Rui; Rui relied on favor and acted despotically—when memorials or orders displeased him, he would tear them up before Yanguang.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Yanguang had long delegated commission business to Yuan Sui and Sun Rui, his left chief adjutant. Sun Rui traded on imperial favor and ran roughshod over others; whenever a dispatch or memorial displeased him, he tore it up in Yanguang's presence.

sentences.zh: 會延光病經旬，銳密召澶州刺史馮暉，與之合謀逼延光反；

translations.literal: When Yanguang fell ill for more than ten days, Rui secretly summoned Feng Hui, military governor of Chan Prefecture, and with him plotted to force Yanguang to rebel;
translations.idiomatic: When Yanguang fell ill for ten days, Rui secretly summoned Feng Hui, governor of Chan Prefecture, and together they plotted to compel Yanguang to rebel;

sentences.zh: 延光亦思張生之言，遂從之。

translations.literal: Yanguang also recalled Master Zhang's words and thereupon joined them.
translations.idiomatic: Yanguang, remembering the diviner Zhang's prophecy, agreed to join them.

sentences.zh: 甲午，六宅使張言奉使魏州還，言延光反狀；

translations.literal: On jiawu, Commissioner of the Six Residences Zhang Yan, returning from a mission to Weizhou, reported Yanguang's rebellion;
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu, Zhang Yan of the Six Residences, back from a mission to Weizhou, reported that Yanguang had rebelled;

sentences.zh: 義成節度使符彥饒奏延光遣兵渡河，焚草市；

translations.literal: Fu Yanrao, military governor of Yicheng, memorialized that Yanguang had sent troops across the river and burned the riverside markets;
translations.idiomatic: Fu Yanrao, governor of Yicheng, reported that Yanguang had sent troops across the Yellow River and burned the riverside markets;

sentences.zh: 詔侍衛馬軍都指揮使、昭信節度使白奉進將千五百騎屯白馬津以備之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Bai Fengjin, commander of the Palace Horse Army and military governor of Zhaoxin, to lead fifteen hundred horsemen to garrison Baima Ford as a precaution.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Bai Fengjin, commander of the palace horse guard and governor of Zhaoxin, to take fifteen hundred cavalry to Baima Ford in readiness.

sentences.zh: 奉進，雲州人也。

translations.literal: Fengjin was a man of Yun Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Fengjin was a native of Yun Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，以東都巡檢使張從賓為魏府西南面都部署。

translations.literal: On dingyou, Zhang Congbin, eastern capital inspection commissioner, was appointed overall commander on the southwest of the Wei commission.
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou, Zhang Congbin, the eastern capital inspection commissioner, was made overall commander on the southwestern front against Wei.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，遣侍衛都軍使楊光遠將步騎一萬屯滑州。

translations.literal: On wuxu, Palace Guard commander Yang Guangyuan was dispatched with ten thousand infantry and cavalry to garrison Huazhou.
translations.idiomatic: On wuxu, Yang Guangyuan, commander of the palace guard, was sent with ten thousand foot and horse to garrison Huazhou.

sentences.zh: 己亥，遣護聖都指揮使杜重威將兵屯衛州。

translations.literal: On jihai, Protective Sage commander Du Chongwei was dispatched with troops to garrison Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: On jihai, Du Chongwei, commander of the Protective Sage guard, was sent to garrison Weizhou with his troops.

sentences.zh: 重威，朔州人也，尚帝妹樂平長公主。

translations.literal: Chongwei was a man of Shuo Prefecture and had married the emperor's younger sister, the Princess of Chang of Leping.
translations.idiomatic: Chongwei was from Shuo Prefecture and had married the emperor's sister, the Princess of Chang of Leping.

sentences.zh: 范延光以馮暉為都部署，孫銳為兵馬都監，將步騎二萬循河西抵黎陽口。

translations.literal: Fan Yanguang appointed Feng Hui overall commander and Sun Rui overseer of troops and horses, and with twenty thousand infantry and cavalry marched along the west bank of the river to reach Liyang Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Yanguang made Feng Hui his overall commander and Sun Rui overseer of troops and horses, then marched twenty thousand men along the west bank of the Yellow River to Liyang Pass.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，楊光遠奏引兵逾胡梁渡。

translations.literal: On xinchou, Yang Guangyuan memorialized that he had led his troops across Huliang Ford.
translations.idiomatic: On xinchou, Yang Guangyuan reported that he had crossed Huliang Ford with his army.

sentences.zh: 以翰林學士、禮部侍郎和凝為端明殿學士。

translations.literal: He Ning, Hanlin academician and vice minister of rites, was appointed academician of the Duanming Hall.
translations.idiomatic: He Ning, Hanlin academician and vice minister of rites, was appointed to the Duanming Hall.

sentences.zh: 凝署其門，不通賓客。

translations.literal: Ning posted a notice on his gate and received no guests.
translations.idiomatic: Ning posted a notice on his gate and refused all visitors.

sentences.zh: 前耀州團練推官襄邑張誼致書於凝，以為「切近之職為天子耳目，宜知四方利病，奈何拒絕賓客！

translations.literal: Zhang Yi of Xiangyi, former investigating officer of the Tuanlian command of Yao Prefecture, wrote to Ning, arguing, "An office so close to the throne serves as the Son of Heaven's eyes and ears; one ought to know the gains and ills of the four quarters—why shut out guests!
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yi of Xiangyi, formerly an investigating officer under Yao Prefecture's training commissioner, wrote to Ning: "A post this close to the throne is the emperor's eyes and ears; you ought to hear what helps and harms the realm from every quarter—yet you shut your door to callers!

sentences.zh: 雖安身為便，如負國何！」

translations.literal: Though it may be convenient for personal safety, what of one's debt to the state!"
translations.idiomatic: Personal comfort is one thing, but what of your duty to the realm!"

sentences.zh: 凝奇之，薦於桑維翰，未幾，除左拾遺。

translations.literal: Ning found him remarkable, recommended him to Sang Weihan, and before long Yi was appointed Left Remonstrance Official.
translations.idiomatic: Ning was impressed, recommended him to Sang Weihan, and before long Zhang Yi was appointed Left Remonstrance Official.

sentences.zh: 誼上言：「北狄有援立之功，宜外敦信好，內謹邊備，不可自逸，以啟戎心。」

translations.literal: Yi memorialized, "The northern barbarians rendered us service in establishing the throne; outwardly we should cultivate good faith and friendship, inwardly we should carefully strengthen border defenses—we must not grow complacent and stir their martial appetite."
translations.idiomatic: Yi submitted a memorial: "The Khitans helped us to the throne; we should treat them with outward cordiality while tightening our frontier defenses inwardly. We must not grow complacent and give them reason to covet our lands."

sentences.zh: 帝深然之。

translations.literal: The emperor strongly agreed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wholeheartedly agreed.

sentences.zh: 契丹攻雲州，半歲不能下。

translations.literal: The Khitans attacked Yun Prefecture and could not take it for half a year.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitans besieged Yun Prefecture for half a year without success.

sentences.zh: 吳巒遣使間道奉表求救，帝為之致書契丹主請之，契丹主乃命翟璋解圍去。

translations.literal: Wu Luan sent an envoy by a hidden route with a memorial seeking relief; the emperor wrote on his behalf to the Khitan sovereign to intercede, and the Khitan sovereign thereupon ordered Zhai Zhang to lift the siege and withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Luan sent an envoy by a secret route with a plea for help; the emperor wrote to the Khitan ruler on his behalf, and the Khitan ruler ordered Zhai Zhang to raise the siege and withdraw.

sentences.zh: 帝召巒歸，以為武寧節度副使。

translations.literal: The emperor summoned Luan back and appointed him deputy military governor of Wuning.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor recalled Luan and made him deputy governor of Wuning.

sentences.zh: 丁未，以侍衛使光遠為魏府四面都部署，張從賓為副部署兼諸軍都虞侯，昭義節度使高行周將本軍屯相州，為魏府西面都部署。

translations.literal: On dingwei, Yang Guangyuan, palace guard commander, was appointed overall commander on all four sides of the Wei commission; Zhang Congbin was made deputy overall commander and chief controller of all armies; Gao Xingzhou, military governor of Zhaoyi, led his own army to garrison Xiang Prefecture as overall commander on the western side of the Wei commission.
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei, Yang Guangyuan was made overall commander on all four sides of the Wei front; Zhang Congbin was his deputy and chief controller of all armies; Gao Xingzhou, governor of Zhaoyi, took his own troops to Xiang Prefecture as western commander against Wei.

sentences.zh: 軍士郭威舊隸劉知遠，當從楊光遠北征，白知遠乞留。

translations.literal: The soldier Guo Wei had formerly served under Liu Zhiyuan; he was to accompany Yang Guangyuan on the northern campaign, but informed Zhiyuan and asked to remain.
translations.idiomatic: The soldier Guo Wei had once served under Liu Zhiyuan; assigned to Yang Guangyuan's northern campaign, he asked Zhiyuan to keep him behind.

sentences.zh: 人問其故，威曰：「楊公有奸詐之才，無英雄之氣，得我何用？

translations.literal: When people asked his reason, Wei said, "Master Yang has a cunning mind but no heroic spirit—what use would he make of me?
translations.idiomatic: Asked why, Wei said, "Yang has a schemer's wit but no hero's breadth—what would he do with me?

sentences.zh: 能用我者其劉公乎！」

translations.literal: The one who could use me properly would be Master Liu!"
translations.idiomatic: Only Liu would know what to do with me!"

sentences.zh: 詔張從賓發河南兵數千人擊范延光。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Zhang Congbin to mobilize several thousand Henan troops to attack Fan Yanguang.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Zhang Congbin to mobilize several thousand Henan troops against Fan Yanguang.

sentences.zh: 延光使人誘從賓，從賓遂與之同反，殺皇子河陽節度使重信，使上將軍張繼祚知河陽留後。

translations.literal: Yanguang sent men to entice Congbin; Congbin thereupon joined him in rebellion, killed the imperial prince Chongxin, military governor of Heyang, and had Senior General Zhang Jizuo serve as acting prefect of Heyang.
translations.idiomatic: Yanguang sent agents to win Congbin over; Congbin joined the rebellion, killed the prince Chongxin, governor of Heyang, and installed Senior General Zhang Jizuo as acting governor of Heyang.

sentences.zh: 繼祚，全義之子也。

translations.literal: Jizuo was a son of Zhang Quanyi.
translations.idiomatic: Jizuo was Zhang Quanyi's son.

sentences.zh: 從賓又引兵入洛陽，殺皇子權東都留守重乂，以東都副留守、都巡檢使張延播知河南府事。

translations.literal: Congbin then led troops into Luoyang, killed the imperial prince Chongyi, acting eastern capital regent, and had Zhang Yanbo, deputy eastern capital regent and chief inspection commissioner, administer Henan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Congbin then marched into Luoyang, killed the prince Chongyi, who had been acting regent of the eastern capital, and put Zhang Yanbo, deputy regent and chief inspection commissioner, in charge of Henan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 從賓取內庫錢帛以賞部兵，留守判官李遐不與，兵眾殺之。

translations.literal: Congbin took money and silk from the inner treasury to reward his troops; Li Xia, staff judge of the regent, refused to comply, and the soldiers killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Congbin seized money and silk from the inner treasury to pay his troops; Li Xia, the regent's staff judge, refused to authorize the disbursement, and the soldiers killed him.

sentences.zh: 從賓引兵東扼汜水關，將逼汴州。

translations.literal: Congbin led troops east to seize Sishui Pass and was about to threaten Bian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Congbin marched east to seize Sishui Pass, poised to threaten the capital at Bian.

sentences.zh: 詔奉國都指揮使侯益帥益兵五千會杜重威討張從賓；

translations.literal: An edict ordered Hou Yi, commander of the Fengguo guard, to lead five thousand additional troops to join Du Chongwei in suppressing Zhang Congbin;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Hou Yi, commander of the Fengguo guard, to bring five thousand additional troops to join Du Chongwei against Zhang Congbin;

sentences.zh: 又詔宣徽使劉處讓自黎陽分兵討之。

translations.literal: Another edict ordered Liu Churang, commissioner of the palace insignia, to divide his forces from Liyang to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: He also ordered Liu Churang, commissioner of the palace insignia, to detach troops from Liyang against Congbin.

sentences.zh: 時羽檄縱橫，從官在大梁者無不恟懼，獨桑維翰從容指畫軍事，神色自若，接對賓客，不改常度，眾心差安。

translations.literal: At the time urgent dispatches crisscrossed the realm; every attendant at Daliang was alarmed, but Sang Weihan alone calmly directed military affairs, his bearing unchanged; he received guests as usual, and hearts were somewhat calmed.
translations.idiomatic: Urgent dispatches flooded the capital; every courtier at Daliang was terrified—except Sang Weihan, who calmly directed military affairs as if nothing were amiss, received guests in his usual manner, and thereby steadied men's minds.

sentences.zh: 方士言於閩主，雲有白龍夜見螺峰；

translations.literal: A Daoist adept told the lord of Min that a white dragon had been seen at night on Luofeng;
translations.idiomatic: A Daoist adept told the lord of Min that a white dragon had appeared by night on Luofeng Peak;

sentences.zh: 閩主作白龍寺。

translations.literal: The lord of Min built White Dragon Temple.
translations.idiomatic: The lord of Min built the White Dragon Temple.

sentences.zh: 時百役繁興，用度不足，閩主謂吏部侍郎、判三司候官蔡守蒙曰：「聞有司除官皆受賂，有諸？」

translations.literal: At the time corvée projects multiplied and revenue fell short; the lord of Min said to Cai Shoumeng, vice minister of personnel and acting head of the Three Offices, "I hear that in every appointment officials take bribes—is this so?"
translations.idiomatic: Public works multiplied and funds ran short; the lord of Min asked Cai Shoumeng, vice minister of personnel and acting head of the Three Offices: "I hear every appointment is bought with bribes—is that true?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「浮言無足信也。」

translations.literal: He replied, "Idle talk is not worth believing."
translations.idiomatic: Shoumeng replied, "That is idle rumor, unworthy of belief."

sentences.zh: 閩主曰：「朕知之久矣，今以委卿，擇賢而授，不肖及罔冒者勿拒，第令納賂，籍而獻之。」

translations.literal: The lord of Min said, "I have known of this for a long time; I now entrust it to you—choose the worthy for appointment, do not refuse the unworthy or impostors, only require them to pay bribes, record them, and submit the proceeds."
translations.idiomatic: The lord said, "I have known it for years. I entrust the matter to you: appoint the worthy when you can, but do not turn away the unworthy or the fraudulent—simply take their bribes, record them, and hand the money over to me."

sentences.zh: 守蒙素廉，以為不可；

translations.literal: Shoumeng had always been upright and considered this impossible;
translations.idiomatic: Shoumeng, who had always been honest, thought this unconscionable;

sentences.zh: 閩主怒，守蒙懼而從之。

translations.literal: the lord of Min grew angry, and Shoumeng, in fear, complied.
translations.idiomatic: the lord flew into a rage, and Shoumeng, terrified, complied.

sentences.zh: 自是除官但以貨多寡為差。

translations.literal: From then on appointments were made solely according to the size of the bribe.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth offices went to the highest bidder.

sentences.zh: 閩主又以空名堂牒使醫工陳究賣官於外，專務聚斂，無有盈厭。

translations.literal: The lord of Min also used blank commission scrolls to have the physician Chen Jiu sell offices abroad, devoting himself entirely to accumulation, never satisfied.
translations.idiomatic: The lord also gave blank appointment scrolls to the physician Chen Jiu to sell offices abroad, hoarding wealth without end.

sentences.zh: 又詔民有隱年者杖背，隱口者死，逃亡者族。

translations.literal: An edict also decreed that those who concealed age would be beaten on the back, those who concealed dependents would be executed, and fugitives would have their clans exterminated.
translations.idiomatic: He further decreed that concealing one's age earned a beating, concealing dependents meant death, and flight meant the extermination of one's entire clan.

sentences.zh: 果菜雞豚，皆重征之。

translations.literal: Fruit, vegetables, chickens, and pigs were all heavily taxed.
translations.idiomatic: Even fruit, vegetables, chickens, and pigs were taxed heavily.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，張從賓攻汜水，殺巡檢使宋廷浩。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, Zhang Congbin attacked Sishui and killed inspection commissioner Song Tinghao.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn, Zhang Congbin attacked Sishui and killed the inspection commissioner Song Tinghao.

sentences.zh: 帝戎服，嚴輕騎，將奔晉陽以避之。

translations.literal: The emperor donned armor, assembled light cavalry, and was about to flee to Jinyang to escape.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor donned armor, mustered light cavalry, and prepared to flee to Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 桑維翰叩頭苦諫曰：「賊鋒雖盛，勢不能久，請少待之，不可輕動。」

translations.literal: Sang Weihan kowtowed and urgently remonstrated, saying, "Though the rebels' momentum is strong, it cannot last—please wait a little; do not act rashly."
translations.idiomatic: Sang Weihan kowtowed and pleaded urgently: "The rebels are fierce but cannot endure—wait a little longer; do not stir prematurely."

sentences.zh: 帝乃止。

translations.literal: The emperor then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor held his ground.

sentences.zh: 范延光遣使以蠟丸招誘失職者，右武衛上將軍婁繼英、右衛大將軍尹暉在大梁，溫韜之子延浚、延沼、延袞居許州，皆應之。

translations.literal: Fan Yanguang sent envoys with wax-sealed pellets to recruit men out of office; Guard General of the Right Wuwei Lou Jiying and Major General of the Right Guard Yin Hui were at Daliang; Wen Tao's sons Yanjun, Yanzhao, and Yangun were at Xuzhou—all responded.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Yanguang sent wax-sealed messages to recruit the disaffected; Lou Jiying, Guard General of the Right Wuwei, and Yin Hui, Major General of the Right Guard, were at Daliang; Wen Tao's sons Yanjun, Yanzhao, and Yangun were at Xuzhou—all answered his call.

sentences.zh: 延光令延浚兄弟取許州，聚徒已及千人。

translations.literal: Yanguang ordered the Yanjun brothers to seize Xuzhou; they had already gathered more than a thousand followers.
translations.idiomatic: Yanguang ordered the Yan brothers to take Xuzhou; they had already raised more than a thousand men.

sentences.zh: 繼英、暉事洩，皆出走，壬子，敕以延光奸謀，誣污忠良，自今獲延光諜人，賞獲者，殺諜人，禁蠟書，勿以聞。

translations.literal: Jiying's and Hui's involvement leaked out and both fled; on renzi, an edict stated that because of Yanguang's treacherous plotting and slander of the loyal, from now on when Yanguang's spies were captured, the captor would be rewarded, the spy executed, wax letters forbidden, and none of this need be reported.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiying's and Hui's involvement leaked, both fled; on renzi an edict declared that Yanguang's treachery had slandered the loyal—henceforth anyone capturing one of his spies would be rewarded, the spy executed, wax messages forbidden, and no report required.

sentences.zh: 暉將奔吳，為人所殺。

translations.literal: Hui was about to flee to Wu but was killed by someone.
translations.idiomatic: Hui was heading for Wu when someone killed him.

sentences.zh: 繼英奔許州，依溫氏。

translations.literal: Jiying fled to Xuzhou and took refuge with the Wen clan.
translations.idiomatic: Jiying fled to Xuzhou and threw in his lot with the Wens.

sentences.zh: 忠武節度使萇從簡盛為之備，延浚等不得發，欲殺繼英以自明，延沼止之，遂同奔張從賓。

translations.literal: Chang Congjian, military governor of Zhongwu, made thorough preparations; Yanjun and the others could not launch their revolt, wished to kill Jiying to clear themselves, but Yanzhao stopped them, and they all fled together to Zhang Congbin.
translations.idiomatic: Chang Congjian, governor of Zhongwu, stood ready; the Yan brothers could not move against Xuzhou and wanted to kill Jiying to prove their loyalty, but Yanzhao dissuaded them, and all fled to Zhang Congbin.

sentences.zh: 繼英知其謀，勸從賓執三溫，皆斬之。

translations.literal: Jiying learned of their plot, urged Congbin to seize the three Wens, and all three were beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Forewarned, Jiying urged Congbin to seize the three Wens; all three were executed.

sentences.zh: 白奉進在滑州，軍士有夜掠者，捕之，獲五人；

translations.literal: Bai Fengjin was at Huazhou; soldiers were plundering at night; he captured them and seized five men;
translations.idiomatic: At Huazhou, Bai Fengjin caught five soldiers on a nighttime raid;

sentences.zh: 其三隸奉進，其二隸符彥饒，奉進皆斬之；

translations.literal: three belonged to Fengjin and two to Fu Yanrao; Fengjin executed all of them;
translations.idiomatic: three served under Fengjin and two under Fu Yanrao; Fengjin executed all five;

sentences.zh: 彥饒以其不先白己，甚怒。

translations.literal: Yanrao was greatly angered that Fengjin had not informed him first.
translations.idiomatic: Yanrao was furious that Fengjin had not consulted him first.

sentences.zh: 明日，奉進從數騎詣彥饒謝，彥饒曰：「軍中各有部分，奈何取滑州軍士並斬之，殊無客主之義乎！」

translations.literal: The next day Fengjin came with several horsemen to apologize to Yanrao; Yanrao said, "Each army has its own section—why execute soldiers of Huazhou together, with no regard for host and guest!"
translations.idiomatic: Next day Fengjin rode over with a small escort to apologize; Yanrao said, "Each army has its own chain of command—why execute Huazhou soldiers without so much as a word to me, as if there were no distinction between host and guest!"

sentences.zh: 奉進曰：「軍士犯法，何有彼我！

translations.literal: Fengjin said, "When soldiers break the law, what distinction is there between yours and mine!
translations.idiomatic: Fengjin replied, "Law-breaking soldiers are law-breaking soldiers—what difference between yours and mine!

sentences.zh: 僕已引咎謝公，而公怒不解，豈非欲與延光同反邪！」

translations.literal: I have already acknowledged fault and apologized to you, yet your anger is not assuaged—do you not wish to rebel with Yanguang!"
translations.idiomatic: I have already apologized, yet your fury will not abate—are you not planning to join Yanguang's rebellion!"

sentences.zh: 拂衣而起，彥饒不留；

translations.literal: He shook out his robes and rose; Yanrao did not detain him;
translations.idiomatic: He turned on his heel to leave; Yanrao made no move to stop him;

sentences.zh: 帳下甲士大噪，擒奉進，殺之。

translations.literal: armored soldiers under the tent raised a great clamor, seized Fengjin, and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: armored men in the tent erupted in uproar, seized Fengjin, and killed him.

sentences.zh: 從騎走出，大呼於外，諸軍爭擐甲操兵，喧噪不可禁止。

translations.literal: His escort ran out and shouted loudly outside; the various armies scrambled to don armor and seize weapons, and the uproar could not be stopped.
translations.idiomatic: His escort burst outside shouting; units everywhere grabbed armor and weapons until the din was uncontrollable.

sentences.zh: 奉國左廂都指揮使馬萬惶惑不知所為，帥步兵欲從亂，遇右廂都指揮使盧順密帥部出營，厲聲謂萬曰：「符公擅殺白公，必與魏城通謀。

translations.literal: Ma Wan, left wing commander of Fengguo, bewildered and not knowing what to do, led infantry intending to join the turmoil; he met Lu Shunmi, right wing commander, leading his unit out of camp, who shouted fiercely to Wan, "Lord Fu killed Lord Bai on his own authority—he must be in league with the rebels at Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Wan, commander of the Fengguo left wing, stood bewildered and was about to lead his infantry into the mutiny when Lu Shunmi, commander of the right wing, marched his men out of camp and shouted at him: "Fu murdered Bai on his own authority—he must be in league with the rebels at Wei.

sentences.zh: 此去行宮才二百里，吾輩及軍士家屬皆在大梁，奈何不思報國，乃欲助亂，自求族滅乎！

translations.literal: The traveling palace is only two hundred li from here; our families and those of the soldiers are all at Daliang—why do you not think of serving the state but wish to aid rebellion and bring extermination on your clan!
translations.idiomatic: The traveling palace is only two hundred li away; our families and every soldier's kin are at Daliang—will you not serve the throne but aid mutiny and invite the slaughter of your clans!

sentences.zh: 今日當共擒符公，送天子，立大功。

translations.literal: Today we should together seize Lord Fu, deliver him to the Son of Heaven, and win great merit.
translations.idiomatic: Today we seize Fu, deliver him to the emperor, and win great merit.

sentences.zh: 軍士從命者賞，違命者誅，勿復疑也！」

translations.literal: Soldiers who obey will be rewarded; those who disobey will be executed—do not doubt further!"
translations.idiomatic: Obey and be rewarded; disobey and die—no more hesitation!"

sentences.zh: 萬部兵尚有呼躍者，順密殺數人，眾莫敢動。

translations.literal: Among Wan's troops some still cheered and leaped; Shunmi killed several men, and none dared stir.
translations.idiomatic: Some of Wan's men still shouted and surged forward; Shunmi killed several, and the rest froze.

sentences.zh: 萬不得已從之，與奉國都虞侯方太等共攻牙城，執彥饒，令太部送大梁。

translations.literal: Wan had no choice but to follow; together with Fang Tai, chief controller of Fengguo, and others he attacked the headquarters compound, seized Yanrao, and ordered Tai to escort him to Daliang.
translations.idiomatic: Wan had no choice; with Fang Tai, chief controller of Fengguo, and others he stormed the headquarters, seized Yanrao, and sent Tai to escort him to Daliang.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，敕斬彥饒於班荊館，其兄弟皆不問。

translations.literal: On jiayin, an edict ordered Yanrao beheaded at Banjing Lodge; his brothers were not pursued.
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin, Yanrao was beheaded at Banjing Lodge by imperial order; his brothers went unpunished.

sentences.zh: 楊光遠自白皋引兵趣滑州，士卒聞滑州亂，欲推光遠為主。

translations.literal: Yang Guangyuan led troops from Baigao toward Huazhou; when the soldiers heard of the turmoil at Huazhou, they wished to make Guangyuan their leader.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Guangyuan marched from Baigao toward Huazhou; hearing of the mutiny there, his soldiers tried to proclaim him their chief.

sentences.zh: 光遠曰：「天子豈汝輩販弄之物！

translations.literal: Guangyuan said, "The Son of Heaven is not a commodity for you lot to trade!
translations.idiomatic: Guangyuan cried, "The emperor is not a bauble for you to peddle!

sentences.zh: 晉陽之降出於窮迫，今若改圖，真反賊也！」

translations.literal: The surrender at Jinyang came from desperate straits; if you change course now, you are true rebels!"
translations.idiomatic: We surrendered at Jinyang from necessity; turn traitor now and you are rebels in earnest!"

sentences.zh: 其下乃不敢言。

translations.literal: His subordinates then dared not speak.
translations.idiomatic: His men fell silent.

sentences.zh: 時魏、孟、滑三鎮繼叛，人情大震，帝問計於劉知遠，對曰：「帝者之興，自有天命。

translations.literal: At the time Wei, Meng, and Hua circuits rebelled in succession; popular sentiment was greatly shaken; the emperor asked Liu Zhiyuan for counsel, and he replied, "The rise of an emperor follows Heaven's mandate.
translations.idiomatic: With Wei, Meng, and Hua in succession rebellion, panic spread; the emperor asked Liu Zhiyuan's counsel, and he answered: "Emperors rise by Heaven's mandate.

sentences.zh: 陛下昔在晉陽，糧不支五日，俄成大業。

translations.literal: Your Majesty was once at Jinyang with provisions for less than five days, yet soon achieved the great enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: At Jinyang Your Majesty had provisions for less than five days, yet soon won the throne.

sentences.zh: 今天下已定，內有勁兵，北結強虜，鼠輩何能為乎！

translations.literal: Today the realm is settled, within we have strong armies, to the north we are allied with a powerful foe—what can vermin do!
translations.idiomatic: The realm is settled, our armies are strong, and we are allied with the Khitans in the north—what can these rats accomplish!

sentences.zh: 願陛下撫將相以恩，臣請戢士卒以威；

translations.literal: I wish Your Majesty to treat generals and ministers with kindness; I ask to restrain the soldiers with severity;
translations.idiomatic: Treat your generals and ministers with kindness, Your Majesty; leave it to me to discipline the soldiers with terror;

sentences.zh: 恩威兼著，京邑自安，本根深固，則枝葉不傷矣。」

translations.literal: when kindness and severity are both evident, the capital will be secure of itself; when the root is firm, the branches will not be harmed."
translations.idiomatic: kindness and severity together will calm the capital; firm the root and the branches will not suffer."

sentences.zh: 知遠乃嚴設科禁，宿衛諸軍無敢犯者。

translations.literal: Zhiyuan then established strict regulations and prohibitions, and none of the palace guard armies dared violate them.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiyuan imposed strict discipline, and none of the palace guards dared breach it.

sentences.zh: 有軍士盜紙錢一帕，主者擒之，左右請釋之，知遠曰：「吾誅其情，不計其直。」

translations.literal: A soldier stole a bundle of paper money; the officer in charge seized him; those nearby asked that he be released; Zhiyuan said, "I punish the intent, not the value."
translations.idiomatic: A soldier stole a bundle of spirit money; the guard who caught him asked to let him go; Zhiyuan said, "I punish the crime, not the price."

sentences.zh: 竟殺之。

translations.literal: In the end he had him executed.
translations.idiomatic: He had the man executed anyway.

sentences.zh: 由是眾皆畏服。

translations.literal: From this all were awed into submission.
translations.idiomatic: After that everyone submitted in fear.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，以楊光遠為魏府行營都招討使、兼知行府事，以昭義節度使高行周為河南尹、東京留守，以杜重威為昭義節度使、充侍衛馬軍都指揮使，以侯益為河陽節度使。

translations.literal: On yimao, Yang Guangyuan was appointed overall pacification commissioner of the Wei commission field headquarters and concurrently acting prefect of the commission; Gao Xingzhou, military governor of Zhaoyi, was made prefect of Henan and eastern capital regent; Du Chongwei was made military governor of Zhaoyi and commander of the Palace Horse Army; Hou Yi was made military governor of Heyang.
translations.idiomatic: On yimao, Yang Guangyuan was made overall pacification commissioner at the Wei front and acting commission prefect; Gao Xingzhou, governor of Zhaoyi, became prefect of Henan and regent of the eastern capital; Du Chongwei took Zhaoyi and command of the palace horse guard; Hou Yi became governor of Heyang.

sentences.zh: 帝以渭州奏事皆馬萬為首，擢萬為義成節度使。

translations.literal: The emperor, because reports from Weizhou all credited Ma Wan first, promoted Wan to military governor of Yicheng.
translations.idiomatic: Because Weizhou's reports credited Ma Wan first, the emperor promoted him to governor of Yicheng.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，以盧順密為果州團練使，方太為趙州刺史；

translations.literal: On bingchen, Lu Shunmi was appointed training commissioner of Guo Prefecture and Fang Tai prefect of Zhao Prefecture;
translations.idiomatic: On bingchen, Lu Shunmi was made training commissioner of Guo Prefecture and Fang Tai prefect of Zhao;

sentences.zh: 既而知皆順密之功也，更以順密為昭義留後。

translations.literal: afterward learning that the credit belonged entirely to Shunmi, Shunmi was further made acting military governor of Zhaoyi.
translations.idiomatic: learning soon afterward that the credit was Shunmi's alone, the emperor made Shunmi acting governor of Zhaoyi instead.

sentences.zh: 馮暉、孫銳引兵至六明鎮，光遠引之渡河，半渡而擊之，暉、銳眾大敗，多溺死，斬首三千級，暉、銳走還魏。

translations.literal: Feng Hui and Sun Rui led troops to Liuming Post; Guangyuan lured them across the river and struck while they were half across; Hui's and Rui's forces were routed, many drowned, three thousand heads were taken, and Hui and Rui fled back to Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Hui and Sun Rui marched to Liuming Post; Guangyuan baited them across the river and struck mid-crossing; their army was shattered, many drowned, three thousand heads were taken, and Hui and Rui fled back to Wei.

sentences.zh: 杜重威、侯益引兵至汜水，遇張從賓眾萬餘人，與戰，俘斬殆盡，遂克汜水。

translations.literal: Du Chongwei and Hou Yi led troops to Sishui, encountered more than ten thousand of Zhang Congbin's followers, fought them, captured and killed nearly all, and thereupon took Sishui.
translations.idiomatic: Du Chongwei and Hou Yi reached Sishui, met more than ten thousand of Congbin's men, fought them nearly to annihilation, and took the pass.

sentences.zh: 從賓走，乘馬渡河，溺死。

translations.literal: Congbin fled, mounted a horse to cross the river, and drowned.
translations.idiomatic: Congbin fled, tried to swim his horse across the river, and drowned.

sentences.zh: 獲其黨張延播、繼祚、婁繼英，送大梁，斬之，滅其族。

translations.literal: His confederates Zhang Yanbo, Jizuo, and Lou Jiying were captured, sent to Daliang, beheaded, and their clans exterminated.
translations.idiomatic: His allies Zhang Yanbo, Jizuo, and Lou Jiying were captured, sent to Daliang, executed, and their clans wiped out.

sentences.zh: 史館修撰李濤上言，張全義有再造洛邑之功，乞免其族，乃止誅繼祚妻子。

translations.literal: Li Tao, compiler at the History Office, memorialized that Zhang Quanyi had the merit of rebuilding Luoyang and begged exemption for his clan; thereupon only Jizuo's wife and children were spared from execution.
translations.idiomatic: Li Tao of the History Office pleaded that Zhang Quanyi had rebuilt Luoyang and deserved mercy for his clan; the court spared only Jizuo's wife and children.

sentences.zh: 濤，回之族曾孫也。

translations.literal: Tao was a great-great-grandson of the Li clan of Hui.
translations.idiomatic: Tao was a great-great-grandson of the Hui Li clan.

sentences.zh: 詔東都留守司百官悉赴行在。

translations.literal: An edict ordered all officials of the Eastern Capital's left-behind administration to proceed entirely to the imperial traveling residence.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered every official serving in the Eastern Capital's left-behind administration to join the emperor at his field headquarters.

sentences.zh: 楊光遠奏知博州張暉舉城降。

translations.literal: Yang Guangyuan memorialized reporting that Zhang Hui, acting chief of Bozhou, had raised the city and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Guangyuan reported that Zhang Hui, military commissioner of Bozhou, had surrendered the city.

sentences.zh: 安州威和指揮使王暉聞范延光作亂，殺安遠節度使周瑰，自領軍府，欲俟延光勝則附之，敗則渡江奔吳。

translations.literal: Wang Hui, commander of the Weihe regiment at Anzhou, heard that Fan Yanguang had raised rebellion, killed Anyuan military governor Zhou Gui, and took command of the military government himself; he intended to wait—if Yanguang won he would attach himself to him, if defeated he would cross the river and flee to Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Hui, commander of the Weihe regiment at Anzhou, learned that Fan Yanguang had rebelled, killed Military Governor Zhou Gui of Anyuan, and seized the army headquarters. Hui planned to side with Yanguang if he won, but cross the Yangtze and flee to Wu if he lost.

sentences.zh: 帝遣右領軍上將軍李金全將千騎如安州巡檢，許赦王暉以為唐州刺史。

translations.literal: The emperor dispatched Right Palace Guard senior general Li Jinquan to lead a thousand horsemen to Anzhou to inspect; he promised to pardon Wang Hui and appoint him Tangzhou prefect.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Senior General Li Jinquan of the Right Palace Guard with a thousand cavalry to Anzhou on an inspection tour, offering Wang Hui a pardon and appointment as prefect of Tangzhou.

sentences.zh: 范延光知事不濟，歸罪於孫銳而族之，遣使奉表待罪，戊寅，楊光遠以聞，帝不許。

translations.literal: Fan Yanguang knew affairs would not succeed, blamed Sun Rui and executed his entire clan, sent envoys presenting a memorial awaiting punishment; on wuyin, Yang Guangyuan reported it, and the emperor did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing defeat was inevitable, Fan Yanguang pinned the blame on Sun Rui and had his whole clan executed, then sent envoys with a memorial submitting to judgment. On wuyin, Yang Guangyuan forwarded the report, but the emperor refused to accept his surrender.

sentences.zh: 吳同平章事王令謀如金陵勸徐浩受禪，誥讓不受。

translations.literal: Wu co-chief councilor Wang Lingmou went to Jinling to urge Xu Hao to accept the abdication; Hao declined several times and would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Lingmou, co-chief councilor of Wu, traveled to Jinling to persuade Xu Hao to take the throne, but Hao repeatedly refused.

sentences.zh: 山南東道節度使安從進恐王暉奔吳，遣行軍司馬張朏將兵會復州兵於要路邀之。

translations.literal: Shannan East Circuit military governor An Congjin feared Wang Hui would flee to Wu; he dispatched army chief of staff Zhang Fei to lead troops and join Fuzhou troops at a strategic point to intercept him.
translations.idiomatic: An Congjin, military governor of Shannan East Circuit, feared Wang Hui would escape to Wu. He sent his chief of staff Zhang Fei with troops to join forces from Fuzhou at a key crossing and cut Hui off.

sentences.zh: 暉大掠安州，將奔吳，部將胡進殺之。

translations.literal: Hui greatly plundered Anzhou and was about to flee to Wu; his subordinate officer Hu Jin killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Hui looted Anzhou on a grand scale, then set out for Wu—whereupon his subordinate Hu Jin killed him.

sentences.zh: 八月，癸巳，以狀聞。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on guisi, this was reported in a memorial.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on guisi, the events were reported to the throne.

sentences.zh: 李金全至安州，將士之預於亂者數百人，金全說諭，悉遣詣闕；

translations.literal: Li Jinquan arrived at Anzhou; several hundred officers and soldiers who had participated in the disorder—Jinquan persuaded and instructed them, and sent them all to the court;
translations.idiomatic: When Li Jinquan reached Anzhou, he persuaded several hundred officers and men implicated in the uprising to surrender and dispatched them all to the capital.

sentences.zh: 既而聞指揮使武彥和等數十人挾賄甚多，伏兵於野，執而斬之。

translations.literal: Soon after he heard that dozens of men including commander Wu Yanhe carried much bribe money; he placed ambush troops in the wilds, seized them, and beheaded them.
translations.idiomatic: Later he learned that Wu Yanhe and several dozen other commanders were carrying large bribes. He set an ambush along the road, captured them, and had them executed.

sentences.zh: 彥和且死，呼曰：「王暉首惡，天子猶赦之；

translations.literal: Yanhe, on the point of death, cried out: "Wang Hui was the chief culprit, yet the Son of Heaven still pardoned him;
translations.idiomatic: As he faced execution, Yanhe cried out: "Wang Hui was the ringleader, and the emperor pardoned even him—

sentences.zh: 我輩脅從，何罪乎！」

translations.literal: we were coerced followers—what crime is there!"
translations.idiomatic: We were forced to follow him—what crime did we commit!"

sentences.zh: 帝雖知金全之情，掩而不問。

translations.literal: The emperor, though knowing Jinquan's motives, covered it and did not inquire.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor knew what Jinquan had done but chose to look the other way.

sentences.zh: 吳歷陽公濛知吳將亡，甲午，殺守衛軍使王宏。

translations.literal: Wu Prince of Liyang Meng, knowing Wu was about to perish, on jiawu killed Palace Guard commissioner Wang Hong.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing Wu was doomed, Prince Meng of Liyang killed Palace Guard Commissioner Wang Hong on jiawu.

sentences.zh: 宏子勒兵攻濛，濛射殺之。

translations.literal: Hong's son rallied troops to attack Meng; Meng shot and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Hong's son raised troops to avenge his father, but Meng shot him dead.

sentences.zh: 以德勝節度使周本吳之勳舊，引二騎詣廬州，欲依之。

translations.literal: Because Desheng military governor Zhou Ben was an old meritorious servant of Wu, he took two horsemen and went to Luzhou, wishing to rely on him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Ben of Desheng Circuit was a veteran Wu commander, so Meng took two companions and rode to Luzhou seeking his protection.

sentences.zh: 本聞濛至，將見之，其子弘祚固諫，本怒曰：「我家郎君來，何為不使我見！」

translations.literal: Ben heard Meng had arrived and was about to see him; his son Hongzuo strongly remonstrated. Ben angrily said: "Our family's young lord has come—why will you not let me see him!"
translations.idiomatic: When Ben learned Meng had arrived, he prepared to receive him, but his son Hongzuo urgently dissuaded him. Ben flew into a rage: "A kinsman of our house has come—why will you not let me see him!"

sentences.zh: 弘祚合扉不聽本出，使人執濛於外，送江都。

translations.literal: Hongzuo shut the doors and would not let Ben go out; he sent men to seize Meng outside and escort him to Jiangdu.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzuo barred the door and refused to let his father out, then had Meng seized outside and sent under guard to Jiangdu.

sentences.zh: 徐誥遣使稱詔殺濛於採石，追廢為悖逆庶人，絕屬籍。

translations.literal: Xu Hao dispatched envoys claiming an edict to kill Meng at Caishi, posthumously deposed him as a rebellious commoner, and cut him from the imperial register.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Hao sent agents bearing a purported edict to execute Meng at Caishi, posthumously stripped him of rank as a traitorous commoner, and erased him from the lineage rolls.

sentences.zh: 侍衛軍使郭悰殺濛妻子於和州，誥歸罪於悰，貶池州。

translations.literal: Palace Guard commissioner Guo Cong killed Meng's wife and children at Hezhou; Hao blamed Cong and demoted him to Chizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Guard Commissioner Guo Cong murdered Meng's wife and children at Hezhou. Hao pinned the blame on Cong and banished him to Chizhou.

sentences.zh: 乙巳，赦張從賓、符彥饒、王暉之黨，未伏誅者皆不問。

translations.literal: On yisi, those of the factions of Zhang Congbin, Fu Yanrao, and Wang Hui who had not yet been executed were all pardoned and not prosecuted.
translations.idiomatic: On yisi, the court pardoned the surviving followers of Zhang Congbin, Fu Yanrao, and Wang Hui, declaring them beyond further prosecution.

sentences.zh: 梁、唐以來，士民奉使及俘掠在契丹者，悉遣使贖還其家。

translations.literal: Since Liang and Tang times, scholars and commoners sent on missions and those captured and taken to the Khitan—all were dispatched envoys to ransom and return them to their families.
translations.idiomatic: Envoys were sent to ransom every envoy and captive taken by the Khitan since the Liang and Tang eras and restore them to their families.

sentences.zh: 吳司徒、門下侍郎、同平章事、內樞使、忠武節度使王令謀老病無齒，或勸之致仕，令謀曰：「齊王大事未畢，吾何敢自安！」

translations.literal: Wu Grand Secretary, vice director of the Chancellery, co-chief councilor, inner privy commissioner, and Zhongwu military governor Wang Lingmou was old, ill, and toothless; some urged him to retire. Lingmou said: "The Prince of Qi's great affair is not yet finished—how dare I rest at ease!"
translations.idiomatic: Wang Lingmou—Grand Secretary, vice director of the Chancellery, co-chief councilor, inner privy commissioner, and military governor of Zhongwu—was aged, infirm, and toothless. When others urged him to retire, he said: "The Prince of Qi's great undertaking is not yet complete—how can I simply rest easy!"

sentences.zh: 疾亟，力勸徐誥受禪。

translations.literal: His illness became extreme, and he urgently urged Xu Hao to accept the abdication.
translations.idiomatic: As his illness turned critical, he pressed Xu Hao to accept the throne.

sentences.zh: 是月，吳主下詔，禪位於齊。

translations.literal: That month, the Wu ruler issued an edict abdicating the throne to the Prince of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: That month the Wu emperor issued an edict abdicating in favor of the Prince of Qi.

sentences.zh: 李德誠等復詣金陵帥百官勸進，宋齊丘不署表。

translations.literal: Li Decheng and others again went to Jinling leading the hundred officials to urge accession; Song Qiqiu did not sign the memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Li Decheng and others returned to Jinling at the head of the bureaucracy to press for Hao's accession, but Song Qiqiu refused to sign the memorial.

sentences.zh: 九月，癸丑，令謀卒。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on guichou, Lingmou died.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on guichou, Wang Lingmou died.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，以李金全為安遠節度使。

translations.literal: On jiayin, Li Jinquan was appointed Anyuan military governor.
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin, Li Jinquan was made military governor of Anyuan.

sentences.zh: 婁繼英未及葬梁均王而誅死，詔梁故臣右衛上將軍安崇阮與王故妃郭氏葬之。

translations.literal: Lou Jiying, before he could bury the Liang Prince Jun, was executed to death; an edict ordered former Liang minister Right Guard senior general An Chongruan and the prince's former consort Lady Guo to bury him.
translations.idiomatic: Lou Jiying was put to death before he could bury the Liang Prince of Jun. The court ordered the former Liang minister An Chongruan, senior general of the Right Guard, and the prince's widow Lady Guo to see to the burial.

sentences.zh: 丙寅，吳主命江夏王璘奉璽綬於齊。

translations.literal: On bingyin, the Wu ruler ordered Prince of Jiangxia Lin to present the seal and cord to the Prince of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: On bingyin, the Wu emperor commanded Prince Lin of Jiangxia to deliver the imperial seal and cord to the Prince of Qi.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，甲申，齊王誥即皇帝位於金陵，大赦，改元升元，國號唐。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on jiashen, Prince of Qi Hao ascended the throne as emperor at Jinling, proclaimed a general amnesty, changed the era name to Shengyuan, and the state designation to Tang.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on jiashen, Xu Hao took the throne at Jinling as emperor of Tang, proclaimed a general amnesty, and adopted the era name Shengyuan.

sentences.zh: 追尊太祖武王曰武皇帝。

translations.literal: He posthumously honored the founding ancestor King Wu as Emperor Wu.
translations.idiomatic: He posthumously elevated the founding King Wu to Emperor Wu.

sentences.zh: 乙酉，遣右丞相玠奉冊詣吳主，稱受禪老臣誥謹拜稽首上皇帝尊號曰高尚思玄弘古讓皇，宮室、乘輿、服御皆如故，宗廟、正朔、徽章、服色悉從吳制。

translations.literal: On yiyou, he dispatched Right chief minister Jie bearing the patent to the Wu ruler, stating that abdication minister Hao reverently bowed and prostrated to submit the emperor honorific title Gao Shang Si Xuan Hong Gu Rang Huang; palaces, carriages, and attire all remained as before; ancestral temples, calendar, insignia, and colors all followed Wu regulations.
translations.idiomatic: On yiyou, he sent Right Chief Minister Jie with patents to the former Wu emperor, declaring that Hao, as the abdicating minister, reverently offered the honorific "Retired Emperor of Lofty Virtue, Profound Mysticism, and Ancient Magnanimity." The abdicated ruler's palaces, carriages, and raiment were left unchanged, while ancestral rites, the calendar, badges, and court dress still followed Wu usage.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，立徐知證為江王，徐知諤為饒王。

translations.literal: On dinghai, Xu Zhizheng was established as Prince of Jiang, and Xu Zhiyu as Prince of Rao.
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai, Xu Zhizheng was made Prince of Jiang and Xu Zhiyu Prince of Rao.

sentences.zh: 以吳太子璉領平盧節度使、兼中書令，封弘農公。

translations.literal: Wu crown prince Lian was made to concurrently hold Pinglu military governor and chief director of the Secretariat, enfeoffed as Duke of Hongnong.
translations.idiomatic: Wu's former crown prince Yang Lian was appointed military governor of Pinglu and chief director of the Secretariat, with the title Duke of Hongnong.

sentences.zh: 唐主宴群臣於天泉閣，李德誠曰：「陛下應天順人，惟宋齊丘不樂。」

translations.literal: The Tang ruler feasted the ministers at Tianquan Pavilion; Li Decheng said: "Your Majesty accords with Heaven and follows the people—only Song Qiqiu is not pleased."
translations.idiomatic: At a banquet in Tianquan Pavilion, Li Decheng told the Tang emperor: "You have ascended in accord with Heaven and the people—yet Song Qiqiu alone seems displeased."

sentences.zh: 因出齊丘止德誠勸進書，唐主執書不視，曰：「子嵩三十年舊交，必不相負。」

translations.literal: He then produced Qiqiu's letter stopping Decheng's urging memorial; the Tang ruler held the letter without looking and said: "Zisong is a thirty-year-old friend—he will surely not fail me."
translations.idiomatic: He then produced a letter in which Qiqiu had tried to block Decheng's accession memorial. The emperor set it aside unread, saying: "Zisong has been my friend for thirty years—he would never betray me."

sentences.zh: 齊丘頓首謝。

translations.literal: Qiqiu bowed his head in thanks.
translations.idiomatic: Qiqiu kowtowed in gratitude.

sentences.zh: 己丑，唐主表讓皇改東都宮殿名，皆取於仙經。

translations.literal: On jichou, the Tang ruler memorialized that the Retired Emperor change the Eastern Capital palace names, all taken from immortalist scriptures.
translations.idiomatic: On jichou, the Tang emperor petitioned to rename the Eastern Capital palaces for the Retired Emperor, drawing every new name from Daoist scriptures.

sentences.zh: 讓皇常服羽衣，習辟穀術。

translations.literal: The Retired Emperor regularly wore feather robes and practiced grain-abstinence arts.
