translations.idiomatic: The Retired Emperor habitually dressed in Daoist feathered robes and practiced fasting regimens.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，吳宗室建安王珙等十二人皆降爵為公，而加官增邑。

translations.literal: On xinmao, twelve Wu imperial clansmen including Prince of Jian'an Gong all had their ranks reduced to duke, but received added offices and enlarged fiefs.
translations.idiomatic: On xinmao, twelve members of the former Wu royal house, including Prince Gong of Jian'an, were reduced from princely to ducal rank but given additional offices and enlarged fiefs.

sentences.zh: 丙申，以吳同平章事張延翰及門下侍郎張居詠、中書侍郎李建勳並同平章事。

translations.literal: On bingshen, former Wu co-chief councilor Zhang Yanhan and vice directors of the Chancellery Zhang Juyong and Li Jianxun were all made co-chief councilors.
translations.idiomatic: On bingshen, Zhang Yanhan, formerly co-chief councilor of Wu, was joined by Vice Directors Zhang Juyong and Li Jianxun as co-chief councilors.

sentences.zh: 讓皇以唐主上表，致書辭之；

translations.literal: The Retired Emperor, because the Tang ruler had submitted a memorial, sent a letter declining;
translations.idiomatic: The Retired Emperor wrote back declining the proposal after the Tang emperor's memorial;

sentences.zh: 唐主表謝而不改。

translations.literal: the Tang ruler submitted a memorial of thanks but did not change course.
translations.idiomatic: the Tang emperor thanked him in a memorial but made no changes.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，加宋齊丘大司徒。

translations.literal: On dingyou, Song Qiqiu was promoted to Grand Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou, Song Qiqiu was elevated to Grand Secretary.

sentences.zh: 齊丘雖為左丞相，不預政事，心慍懟，聞制詞云「布衣之交」，抗聲曰：「臣為布衣時，陛下為刺史；

translations.literal: Although Qiqiu served as Left chief minister, he did not participate in government affairs; his heart was resentful and indignant. Hearing the appointment text say "friendship in common cloth," he said aloud: "When I was in common cloth, Your Majesty was a prefect;
translations.idiomatic: Though named Left Chief Minister, Qiqiu was excluded from affairs of state and nursed a growing grievance. When the appointment edict spoke of "friendship in humble stations," he cried out: "When I was a commoner, Your Majesty was a prefect—

sentences.zh: 今日為天子，可不用老臣矣。」

translations.literal: today you are Son of Heaven—you need not use this old minister anymore."
translations.idiomatic: now you are emperor, and you clearly have no further use for your old servant."

sentences.zh: 還家請罪，唐主手詔謝之，亦不改命。

translations.literal: He returned home to submit to punishment; the Tang ruler sent a personal edict apologizing, but also did not revise the appointment.
translations.idiomatic: He went home to await punishment. The emperor sent a personal letter of apology but left the appointment unchanged.

sentences.zh: 久之，齊丘不知所出，乃更上書請遷讓皇於它州，及斥遠吳太子璉，絕其婚；

translations.literal: After a long time, not knowing what course to take, Qiqiu again submitted a memorial requesting that the Retired Emperor be moved to another prefecture, and that Wu crown prince Lian be sent far away and his marriage alliance severed;
translations.idiomatic: In time, grasping for leverage, Qiqiu memorialized again—proposing to relocate the Retired Emperor to another province, exile the former Wu crown prince Yang Lian, and break off his marriage alliance.

sentences.zh: 唐主不從。

translations.literal: the Tang ruler did not follow it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor refused both proposals.

sentences.zh: 乙巳，立王后宋氏為皇后。

translations.literal: On yisi, the queen consort, Lady Song, was established as empress.
translations.idiomatic: On yisi, Lady Song, the emperor's consort, was enthroned as empress.

sentences.zh: 戊申，以諸道都統、判元帥府事景通為諸道副元帥、判六軍諸衛事、太尉、尚書令、吳王。

translations.literal: On wushen, circuit-wide commander-in-chief and adjudicator of the Marshal's Office Jingtong was made circuit-wide deputy commander-in-chief, adjudicator of the Six Armies and various guards, Grand Commander, Director of the Department of State Affairs, and Prince of Wu.
translations.idiomatic: On wushen, Jingtong—commander-in-chief of all circuits and head of the Marshal's Office—was made deputy commander-in-chief of all circuits, overseer of the Six Armies and palace guards, Grand Commander, Director of the Department of State Affairs, and Prince of Wu.

sentences.zh: 閩主命其弟威武節度使繼恭上表告嗣位於晉，且請置邸於都下。

translations.literal: The Min ruler ordered his younger brother Weiwu military governor Jigong to submit a memorial announcing succession to Jin, and also requesting establishment of a residence in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: The Min ruler had his brother Jigong, military governor of Weiwu, send a memorial announcing his accession to the Jin court and requesting an official residence in the capital.

sentences.zh: 十一月，乙卯，唐吳王景通更名璟。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on yimao, Tang Prince of Wu Jingtong changed his name to Jing.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on yimao, Prince Jingtong of Wu changed his name to Jing.

sentences.zh: 唐主賜楊璉妃號永興公主；

translations.literal: The Tang ruler bestowed on Yang Lian's consort the title Princess of Yongxing;
translations.idiomatic: The Tang emperor granted Yang Lian's consort the title Princess of Yongxing;

sentences.zh: 妃聞人呼公主則流涕而辭。

translations.literal: when the consort heard people address her as princess, she wept and declined.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing herself addressed as princess, the consort wept and refused the title.

sentences.zh: 戊午，唐主立其子景遂為吉王，景達為壽陽公；

translations.literal: On wuwu, the Tang ruler established his sons Jingsui as Prince of Ji and Jingda as Duke of Shouyang;
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu, the Tang emperor ennobled his sons—Jingsui as Prince of Ji and Jingda as Duke of Shouyang;

sentences.zh: 以景遂為侍中、東都留守、江都尹，帥留司百官赴東都。

translations.literal: Jingsui was made chief director of the Secretariat, Eastern Capital left-behind commissioner, and Jiangdu magistrate, leading the left-behind officials to the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Jingsui was also made chief director of the Secretariat, left-behind commissioner of the Eastern Capital, and magistrate of Jiangdu, and sent at the head of the capital administration to the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 戊辰，詔加吳越王元瓘天下兵馬副元帥，進封吳越國王。

translations.literal: On wuchen, an edict promoted King Yuanzhan of Wuyue to deputy commander-in-chief of all armies under Heaven and advanced his enfeoffment to King of the Wuyue State.
translations.idiomatic: On wuchen, the court promoted King Yuanzhan of Wuyue to deputy commander-in-chief of all forces and raised his title to King of Wuyue.

sentences.zh: 安遠節度使李金全以親吏胡漢筠為中門使，軍府事一以委之。

translations.literal: Anyuan military governor Li Jinquan made his personal clerk Hu Hanjun middle gate commissioner and entrusted all military government affairs entirely to him.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jinquan, military governor of Anyuan, installed his personal aide Hu Hanjun as middle gate commissioner and handed him full control of headquarters affairs.

sentences.zh: 漢筠貪滑殘忍，聚斂無厭。

translations.literal: Hanjun was greedy, slippery, and cruel, amassing levies without satiation.
translations.idiomatic: Hanjun was greedy, ruthless, and insatiably corrupt.

sentences.zh: 帝聞之，以廉吏賈仁沼代之，且召漢筠，欲授以它職，庶保全功臣。

translations.literal: The emperor heard of it and replaced him with upright official Jia Renzhao, and also summoned Hanjun, intending to grant him another office, hoping thereby to preserve the meritorious minister.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor learned of this, he replaced Hanjun with the upright Jia Renzhao and summoned Hanjun to court for reassignment, hoping to shield the aging general from his aide's depredations.

sentences.zh: 漢筠大懼，始勸金全以異謀。

translations.literal: Hanjun was greatly afraid and for the first time urged Jinquan toward divergent designs.
translations.idiomatic: Terrified, Hanjun urged Jinquan toward rebellion for the first time.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，金全表漢筠病，未任行。

translations.literal: On yihai, Jinquan memorialized that Hanjun was ill and could not undertake the journey.
translations.idiomatic: On yihai, Jinquan reported that Hanjun was too ill to travel.

sentences.zh: 金全故人龐令圖屢諫曰：「仁沼忠義之士，以代漢筠，所益多矣。」

translations.literal: Jinquan's old friend Pang Lingtu repeatedly remonstrated, saying: "Renzhao is a loyal and righteous man—to replace Hanjun with him brings much benefit."
translations.idiomatic: Jinquan's old friend Pang Lingtu repeatedly warned him: "Renzhao is a man of loyalty and integrity—replacing Hanjun with him would bring nothing but gain."

sentences.zh: 漢筠夜遣壯士逾垣滅令圖之族，又毒仁沼，舌爛而卒。

translations.literal: Hanjun by night sent stalwart men over the wall to exterminate Lingtu's clan, and also poisoned Renzhao, whose tongue rotted and he died.
translations.idiomatic: That night Hanjun sent bravos over the wall to slaughter Pang Lingtu's entire family. He also poisoned Renzhao, whose tongue rotted away before he died.

sentences.zh: 漢筠與推官張緯相結，以諂惑金全，金全愛之彌篤。

translations.literal: Hanjun joined with legal officer Zhang Wei; by flattery he misled Jinquan, and Jinquan loved him ever more deeply.
translations.idiomatic: Hanjun allied with legal officer Zhang Wei, whose flattery ensnared Jinquan, whom Hanjun came to trust all the more.

sentences.zh: 十二月戊申，蜀大赦，改明年元曰明德。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, wushen, Shu proclaimed a general amnesty and changed next year's era name to Mingde.
translations.idiomatic: On wushen in the twelfth month, Shu proclaimed a general amnesty and renamed the coming year Mingde.

sentences.zh: 詔加馬希範江南諸道都統，制置武平、靜江等軍事。

translations.literal: An edict promoted Ma Xifan to commander-in-chief of the Jiangnan circuits, arranging Wuping, Jingjiang, and other military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The court appointed Ma Xifan commander-in-chief of the Jiangnan circuits with authority over the armies of Wuping, Jingjiang, and neighboring commands.

sentences.zh: 是歲，契丹改元會同，國號大遼，公卿庶官皆仿中國，參用中國人，以趙延壽為樞密使，尋兼政事令。

translations.literal: That year, the Khitan changed the era name to Huitong, the state designation to Great Liao; dukes, ministers, and common officials all imitated China, employing Chinese people concurrently; Zhao Yanshou was made privy commissioner, and soon also held chief administrator of affairs.
translations.idiomatic: That year the Khitan adopted the era name Huitong and the dynastic title Great Liao. Their entire bureaucracy was modeled on Chinese practice, with Chinese officials in key posts. Zhao Yanshou was named privy commissioner and soon added chief administrator of affairs.

sentences.zh: 高祖聖文章武明德孝皇帝上之下天福三年（

translations.literal: Gaozu the Sagely Literary Martial Virtuous Filial Emperor, Part Two Below, Tianfu year 3 (
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu the Sagely Literary Martial Virtuous Filial Emperor, Part Two Below—Tianfu year 3 (

sentences.zh: 戊戌，公元九三八年）

translations.literal: wuxu, AD 938)
translations.idiomatic: wuxu, 938 CE)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，己酉，日有食之。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on jiyou, there was an eclipse of the sun.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on the day jiyou, the sun was eclipsed.

sentences.zh: 唐德勝節度使兼中書令西平恭烈王周本以不能存吳，愧恨而卒。

translations.literal: Tang Desheng military governor and concurrent chief director of the Secretariat, Xiping reverent and fierce King Zhou Ben, because he could not preserve Wu, died of shame and resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Ben—the Desheng military governor, chief director of the Secretariat, and posthumously styled Reverent and Fierce King of Xiping—died consumed by shame and regret that he had failed to save Wu.

sentences.zh: 丙寅，唐以侍中吉王景遂參判尚書都省。

translations.literal: On bingyin, Tang made chief director of the Secretariat Prince of Ji Jingsui participate in adjudicating the Directorate-General of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: On bingyin, Tang appointed Prince Jingsui of Ji, chief director of the Secretariat, to assist in governing the Directorate-General of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 蜀主以武信節度使、同平章事張業為左僕射兼中書侍郎、同平章事、樞密使，武泰節度使王處回兼武信節度使、同平章事。

translations.literal: The Shu ruler made Wuxin military governor and co-chief councilor Zhang Ye Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs with concurrent appointment as vice director of the Secretariat, co-chief councilor, and privy commissioner; Wutai military governor Wang Chuhui was made to concurrently hold Wuxin military governor and co-chief councilor.
translations.idiomatic: The Shu emperor made Zhang Ye—military governor of Wuxin and co-chief councilor—Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, vice director of the Secretariat, co-chief councilor, and privy commissioner, while Wang Chuhui of Wutai Circuit also received Wuxin and a co-chief councilorship.

sentences.zh: 二月，庚辰，左散騎常侍張允上《駁赦論》，以為：「帝王遇天災多肆赦，謂之修德。

translations.literal: In the second month, on gengchen, Left Regular Attendant of the Cavalry Zhang Yun submitted "On Refuting Amnesties," arguing: "When emperors and kings encounter heavenly disasters they often proclaim amnesties, calling it cultivating virtue.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on gengchen, Left Regular Attendant Zhang Yun submitted his "Refutation of Amnesties," arguing: "Emperors facing natural calamities often proclaim general pardons, calling it moral cultivation—

sentences.zh: 借有二人坐獄遇赦，則曲者倖免，直者銜冤，冤氣升聞，乃所以致災，非所以弭災也。」

translations.literal: Suppose two men sit in prison and encounter an amnesty—the crooked one luckily escapes, the upright one harbors grievance; grievance qi rises and is heard—this is what brings disaster, not what quells disaster."
translations.idiomatic: but if two prisoners are pardoned together, the guilty go free while the innocent remain wronged. Resentment then rises to Heaven—the very thing that brings calamity, not the means to end it."

sentences.zh: 詔褒之。

translations.literal: An edict praised him.
translations.idiomatic: The court commended him by edict.

sentences.zh: 帝樂聞讜言，詔百官各上封事，命使部尚書梁文矩等十人置詳定院以考之，無取者留中，可者行之。

translations.literal: The emperor delighted in hearing candid words; he ordered the hundred officials each to submit sealed memorials, and appointed envoy department minister Liang Wenju and nine others to establish a Detailed Review Office to examine them—those with nothing acceptable were kept at court; those acceptable were implemented.
translations.idiomatic: Delighted by such frank counsel, the emperor ordered every official to submit sealed recommendations and appointed Liang Wenju of the Envoy Department and nine others to a Review Office. Worthless submissions were withheld; acceptable ones were put into effect.

sentences.zh: 數月，應詔都無十人，乙未，復降御札趣之。

translations.literal: Several months passed; those responding to the edict did not reach ten people; on yiwei, he again issued an imperial letter urging them.
translations.idiomatic: Months passed with fewer than ten responses. On yiwei, the emperor sent another personal letter urging compliance.

sentences.zh: 三月，丁丑，敕禁民作銅器。

translations.literal: In the third month, on dingchou, an edict forbade the people from making copper vessels.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on dingchou, the court banned the private manufacture of copper wares.

sentences.zh: 初，唐世天下鑄錢有三十六冶，喪亂以來，皆廢絕，錢日益耗，民多銷錢為銅器，故禁之。

translations.literal: Initially, in Tang times throughout the realm there were thirty-six mints for casting coin; since the disorders all had been abandoned and cut off, coin daily grew scarcer, and the people mostly melted coin to make copper vessels—therefore it was forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: Under Tang, thirty-six mints had supplied the empire with coin, but war had shut them all down. As cash grew ever scarcer, people increasingly melted it into copperware—which was why the ban was imposed.

sentences.zh: 中書舍人李詳上疏，以為「十年以來，赦令屢降，諸道職掌皆許推恩，而籓方薦論動逾數百，乃至藏典、書吏、優伶、奴僕，初命則至銀青階，被服皆紫袍象笏，名器僭濫，貴賤不分。

translations.literal: Secretariat drafter Li Xiang submitted a memorial, arguing: "Over the past ten years, amnesty edicts have repeatedly been issued; every circuit office has been permitted to extend favor, yet frontier recommendations and nominations often exceed several hundred—even including archivists, clerks, actors, and slaves; on first appointment they reach silver-and-cyan rank, their garb all purple robes and ivory tablet; titular offices are usurped in excess, noble and base undistinguished.
translations.idiomatic: Secretariat Drafter Li Xiang submitted a memorial arguing that "for a decade repeated amnesties had let every circuit shower favors indiscriminately. Frontier nominations now ran to hundreds—even archivists, clerks, actors, and slaves received initial appointments at silver-and-cyan rank, dressed in purple robes with ivory tablets. Honors meant for the elite had been debased beyond recognition.

sentences.zh: 請自今諸道主兵將校之外，節度州聽奏朱記大將以上十人，他州止聽奏都押牙、都虞候、孔目官，自餘但委本道量遷職名而已。」

translations.literal: He requested that from now on, apart from military commanders of each circuit, military commission prefectures be permitted to memorialize ten persons from red-recorded great generals upward; other prefectures be permitted to memorialize only chief military adjutants, chief military inspectors, and chief clerks; for the rest, let each circuit alone measure and transfer official names."
translations.idiomatic: He proposed that henceforth, beyond frontline commanders, circuit capitals might nominate no more than ten officers of chief commander rank or higher, while ordinary prefectures could nominate only chief adjutants, chief inspectors, and chief clerks—all other promotions to be handled internally without imperial nomination."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: This was followed.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was adopted.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，甲申，唐宋齊丘自陳丞相不應不豫政事，唐主答以省署未備。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on jiashen, Tang's Song Qiqiu personally stated that a chief minister ought not be excluded from government affairs; the Tang ruler replied that provincial and departmental offices were not yet complete.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on jiashen, Song Qiqiu protested that a chief minister should not be shut out of government. The Tang emperor replied that the ministries were not yet fully staffed.

sentences.zh: 吳讓皇固辭舊宮，屢請徙居；

translations.literal: The Wu Retired Emperor firmly declined the old palace and repeatedly requested relocation;
translations.idiomatic: The Retired Emperor of Wu repeatedly refused the old palace and begged to be moved elsewhere;

sentences.zh: 李德誠等亦亟以為言。

translations.literal: Li Decheng and others also urgently spoke on the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Li Decheng and others pressed the point as well.

sentences.zh: 五月，戊午，唐主改潤州牙城為丹楊宮，以李建勳為迎奉讓皇使。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on wuwu, the Tang ruler converted Runzhou's military headquarters city into Danyang Palace and made Li Jianxun commissioner for receiving and escorting the Retired Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on wuwu, the Tang emperor converted Runzhou's headquarters compound into Danyang Palace and appointed Li Jianxun commissioner to receive and escort the Retired Emperor.

sentences.zh: 楊光遠自恃擁重兵，頗干預朝政，屢有抗奏，帝常屈意從之。

translations.literal: Yang Guangyuan, relying on his possession of heavy troops, considerably interfered in court politics; he repeatedly had confrontational memorials, and the emperor often bent his intent to follow him.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Guangyuan, emboldened by his large army, repeatedly intervened in court politics with defiant memorials, and the emperor often yielded to him.

sentences.zh: 庚申，以其子承祚為左威衛將軍，尚帝女長安公主，次子承信亦拜美官，寵冠當時。

translations.literal: On gengshen, his son Chengzuo was made Left Weiwu Guard general and married the emperor's daughter Princess of Chang'an; the second son Chengxin also received a fine office; their favor topped the age.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen, his eldest son Chengzuo was made a general of the Left Weiwu Guard and married the emperor's daughter, Princess of Chang'an; a second son, Chengxin, received a prestigious appointment as well. No family enjoyed greater favor at court.

sentences.zh: 壬戌，唐主以左宣威副統軍王輿為鎮海留後，客省使公孫圭為監軍使，親吏馬思讓為丹楊宮使，徙讓皇居丹楊宮。

translations.literal: On renxu, the Tang ruler made Left Xuanwei deputy commander Wang Yu acting military governor of Zhenhai, reception commissioner Gongsun Gui army supervision commissioner, and personal clerk Ma Sirang Danyang Palace commissioner, relocating the Retired Emperor to reside at Danyang Palace.
translations.idiomatic: On renxu, the Tang emperor installed Wang Yu as acting military governor of Zhenhai, Gongsun Gui as army supervisor, and his personal aide Ma Sirang as keeper of Danyang Palace, then moved the Retired Emperor into Danyang Palace.

sentences.zh: 宋齊丘復自陳為左右所間，唐主大怒；

translations.literal: Song Qiqiu again personally stated that he had been estranged by those at the ruler's side; the Tang ruler was greatly angry;
translations.idiomatic: Song Qiqiu again complained that courtiers had turned the emperor against him, and the Tang ruler flew into a rage.

sentences.zh: 齊丘歸第，白衣待罪。

translations.literal: Qiqiu returned to his residence and awaited punishment in plain white garments.
translations.idiomatic: Qiqiu went home in plain robes to await judgment.

sentences.zh: 或曰：「齊丘舊臣，不宜以小過棄之。」

translations.literal: Someone said: "Qiqiu is an old minister—it is not fitting to discard him for a small fault."
translations.idiomatic: An adviser said: "Qiqiu is a founding minister—it would be wrong to cast him aside over a minor offense."

sentences.zh: 唐主曰：「齊丘有才，不識大體。」

translations.literal: The Tang ruler said: "Qiqiu has talent but does not grasp the larger picture."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied: "Qiqiu is gifted, but he cannot see the bigger picture."

sentences.zh: 乃命吳王璟持手詔召之。

translations.literal: He then ordered Prince of Wu Jing to carry a personal edict summoning him.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Prince Jing of Wu with a personal summons to bring him back.

sentences.zh: 六月，壬午，或獻毒酒方於唐主，唐主曰：「犯吾法者自有常刑，安用此為！」

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on renwu, someone presented a poison-wine formula to the Tang ruler; the Tang ruler said: "Those who violate my law have their own regular punishments—what use is this!
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on renwu, someone offered the Tang emperor a recipe for poisoned wine. He refused: "Those who break my laws face proper punishment—what need have I for this!"

sentences.zh: 群臣爭請改府寺州縣名有吳及楊者，留守判官楊嗣請更姓羊，徐玠曰：「陛下自應天順人，事非逆取，而諂邪之人專事改更，鹹非急務，不可從也。」

translations.literal: The officials all vied to request changing the names of prefectures, offices, prefectures, and counties that contained Wu or Yang; the garrison deputy commissioner Yang Si requested changing his surname to Yang; Xu Jie said: "Your Majesty yourself responded to Heaven and followed the people; the matter was not a usurpation, yet flatterers and the corrupt devote themselves solely to making changes—it is certainly not an urgent task and cannot be followed."
translations.idiomatic: The courtiers clamored to rename every prefecture, office, and county whose name contained Wu or Yang. Garrison deputy commissioner Yang Si even asked to change his surname to Yang—the character for "goat." Xu Jie objected: "Your Majesty came to power in accord with Heaven and the people's will; yours was no usurpation. Yet sycophants fixate on pointless renaming. This is hardly urgent, and Your Majesty should refuse."

sentences.zh: 唐主然之。

translations.literal: The Tang ruler approved of this.
translations.idiomatic: The Tang emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 河南留守高行周奏修洛陽宮。

translations.literal: Henan garrison commander Gao Xingzhou memorialized to repair the Luoyang palace.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Xingzhou, military governor of Henan, memorialized requesting repairs to the Luoyang palace.

sentences.zh: 丙戌，左諫議大夫薛融諫曰：「今宮室雖經焚毀，猶侈於帝堯之茅茨；

translations.literal: On bingxu, Left Remonstrance and Counsellor Xue Rong remonstrated, saying: "Though the palace has been burned and destroyed, it is still more lavish than Emperor Yao's thatched hut;
translations.idiomatic: On bingxu, Left Remonstrance Counsellor Xue Rong urged: "Though the palace has been burned, it would still surpass the thatched hut of Emperor Yao;

sentences.zh: 所費雖寡，猶多於漢文之露台。

translations.literal: Though the expense is small, it is still more than Emperor Wen of Han's open terrace.
translations.idiomatic: and though the cost may seem modest, it would exceed even the open terrace of Emperor Wen of Han.

sentences.zh: 況魏城未下，公私困窘，誠非陛下修宮館之日；

translations.literal: Moreover, since Weicheng has not fallen and public and private affairs are distressed, it is truly not the day for Your Majesty to repair palaces and lodges;
translations.idiomatic: With Wei City still unconquered and the state in straits, this is no time to rebuild palaces and halls;

sentences.zh: 請俟海內平寧，營之未晚。」

translations.literal: Please wait until all within the seas is peaceful and secure—building then would not be late."
translations.idiomatic: wait until the realm is at peace; building then would not be too late."

sentences.zh: 上納其言，仍賜詔褒之。

translations.literal: The emperor accepted his words and still bestowed an edict praising him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took his advice and issued an edict commending him.

sentences.zh: 己丑，金部郎中經鑄奏：「竊見鄉村浮戶，非不勤稼穡，非不樂安居，但以種木未盈十年，墾田未及三頃，似成生業，已為縣司收供徭役，責之重賦，威以嚴刑，故不免捐功捨業，更思他適。

translations.literal: On jichou, Ministry of Revenue section director Jing Zhuo memorialized: "I have privately observed floating households in villages and hamlets—they are not undiligent in sowing and reaping, not unwilling to dwell in peace—but because planted trees have not reached ten years and reclaimed fields have not reached three qing, seeming to have established a livelihood, they are already collected by the county office for corvée labor, charged heavy taxes, and threatened with severe punishments; therefore they cannot avoid abandoning their labor and giving up their livelihood, and instead think of going elsewhere.
translations.idiomatic: On jichou, Jing Zhuo of the Ministry of Revenue memorialized: "I find that migrant households in the countryside are eager to farm and eager to settle down. Yet once they have planted trees for less than ten years or cleared less than three qing of land—barely enough to count as a livelihood—the county presses them into corvée, levies crushing taxes, and threatens harsh punishment. Small wonder they abandon their farms and move on.

sentences.zh: 乞自今民墾田及五頃以上，三年外乃聽縣司徭役。」

translations.literal: I beg that from now on, for people who reclaim fields reaching five qing or more, only after three years beyond that may the county office impose corvée."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that henceforth county officials be barred from imposing corvée until a household has farmed at least five qing for three full years."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: His request was followed.
translations.idiomatic: The request was granted.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，中書奏：「朝代雖殊，條制無異。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, the Secretariat memorialized: "Though dynasties differ, statutes and regulations are not different.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn, the Secretariat reported: "Different dynasties may rise and fall, but their administrative codes are much the same.

sentences.zh: 請委官取明宗及清泰時敕，詳定可久行者編次之。」

translations.literal: Please commission officials to take the edicts from Mingzong's and Qingtai's times, carefully determine those that can be long practiced, and compile and arrange them."
translations.idiomatic: We ask that officials be assigned to collect edicts from the reigns of Mingzong and Qingtai, revise those suited to long-term use, and compile them into a code."

sentences.zh: 己酉，詔左諫議大夫薛融等詳定。

translations.literal: On jiyou, an edict ordered Left Remonstrance and Counsellor Xue Rong and others to compile and determine them in detail.
translations.idiomatic: On jiyou, the emperor ordered Xue Rong and others to undertake the revision.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，敕作受命寶，以「受天明命，惟德允昌」為文。

translations.literal: On xinyou, an edict ordered the making of the Mandate-receiving Seal, with the text "Receiving Heaven's bright mandate—virtue alone brings lasting prosperity."
translations.idiomatic: On xinyou, the emperor ordered a Mandate-receiving Seal cast with the inscription "Having received Heaven's clear mandate, may virtue alone bring enduring glory."

sentences.zh: 八月，帝上尊號於契丹主及太后，戊寅，以馮道為太后冊禮使，左僕射劉昫為契丹主冊禮使，備鹵薄、儀仗、車輅，詣契丹行禮；

translations.literal: In the eighth month, the emperor presented honorific titles to the Khitan ruler and empress dowager; on wuyin, he made Feng Dao empress dowager investiture envoy and Left Vice Director Liu Xu Khitan ruler investiture envoy, fully equipped with halberd guards, ceremonial insignia, and carriages, proceeding to Khitan to perform the rites;
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month the emperor sent honorific titles to the Khitan emperor and empress dowager. On wuyin he appointed Feng Dao envoy to invest the empress dowager and Left Vice Director Liu Xu envoy to invest the Khitan ruler, equipping them with full guard of honor, ceremonial regalia, and imperial carriages for the journey to the Khitan court.

sentences.zh: 契丹主大悅。

translations.literal: The Khitan ruler was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan emperor was delighted.

sentences.zh: 帝事契丹甚謹，奉表稱臣，謂契丹主為「父皇帝」；

translations.literal: The emperor served the Khitan very deferentially, submitted memorials calling himself subject, and addressed the Khitan ruler as "Father Emperor";
translations.idiomatic: The emperor treated the Khitan with scrupulous deference, submitting memorials as a vassal and addressing the Khitan ruler as "Imperial Father";

sentences.zh: 每契丹使至，帝於別殿拜受詔敕。

translations.literal: Whenever Khitan envoys arrived, the emperor in a separate hall bowed to receive edicts and decrees.
translations.idiomatic: whenever Khitan envoys arrived, he received their edicts kneeling in a side hall.

sentences.zh: 歲輸金帛三十萬之外，吉凶慶吊，歲時贈遺，玩好珍異，相繼於道。

translations.literal: Beyond the annual tribute of three hundred thousand in gold and silk, for misfortune and fortune, mourning and congratulation, seasonal gifts, curios and rare treasures—they followed one after another on the road.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond the annual tribute of three hundred thousand units of gold and silk, gifts for every occasion—condolences, congratulations, seasonal offerings, curios and rarities—streamed endlessly along the roads.

sentences.zh: 乃至應天太后、元帥太子、偉王、南、北二王、韓延徽、趙延壽等諸大臣皆有賂遺。

translations.literal: Even to Empress Dowager Yingtian, Crown Prince the Marshal, Prince Wei, the Southern and Northern Princes, Han Yanhui, Zhao Yanshou, and all the great ministers—there were bribes and gifts.
translations.idiomatic: Even the Yingtian Empress Dowager, the crown prince marshal, Prince Wei, the southern and northern princes, Han Yanhui, Zhao Yanshou, and other Khitan grandees received lavish gifts.

sentences.zh: 小不如意，輒來責讓，帝常卑辭謝之。

translations.literal: At the slightest dissatisfaction, they would come to reproach and blame; the emperor often with humble words apologized to them.
translations.idiomatic: At the slightest displeasure they sent envoys to rebuke him, and he invariably answered with abject apologies.

sentences.zh: 晉使者至契丹，契丹驕倨，多不遜語。

translations.literal: When Jin envoys reached Khitan, the Khitan were arrogant and haughty, often using disrespectful speech.
translations.idiomatic: Jin envoys at the Khitan court were met with arrogance and frequent insults.

sentences.zh: 使者還，以聞，朝野鹹以為恥，而帝事之曾無倦意，以是終帝之世，與契丹無隙。

translations.literal: When envoys returned and reported this, court and countryside all regarded it as shameful, yet the emperor in serving them never had any sign of weariness; by this through the end of the emperor's lifetime there was no breach with Khitan.
translations.idiomatic: Envoys returned to report this, and the court and country alike felt humiliated. Yet the emperor never flagged in his deference, and for the rest of his reign Jin and Khitan remained at peace.

sentences.zh: 然所輸金帛不過數縣租賦，往往托以民困，不能滿數。

translations.literal: Yet the gold and silk paid in tribute amounted to no more than several counties' rent and tax levies; often citing the people's distress, they could not fulfill the full amount.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the tribute amounted to only a few counties' tax revenue, and the court often pleaded poverty to pay less than the full sum.

sentences.zh: 其後契丹主屢止帝上表稱臣，但令為書稱「兒皇帝」，如家人禮。

translations.literal: Afterward the Khitan ruler repeatedly stopped the emperor from submitting memorials calling himself subject, only ordering letters addressing himself as "Son Emperor," like family rites.
translations.idiomatic: Later the Khitan emperor repeatedly forbade formal submissions calling Jin his vassal, requiring only letters addressed to him as "Son Emperor"—the etiquette of a household.

sentences.zh: 初，契丹主既得幽州，命曰南京，以唐降將趙思溫為留守。

translations.literal: At the beginning, after the Khitan ruler had obtained Youzhou, he named it Southern Capital and made Tang surrendered general Zhao Siwen garrison commander.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, after taking Youzhou, the Khitan emperor named it the Southern Capital and appointed the Tang defector Zhao Siwen as its military governor.

sentences.zh: 思溫子延照在晉，帝以為祁州刺史。

translations.literal: Siwen's son Yanzhao was in Jin; the emperor made him prefect of Qi Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Siwen's son Yanzhao was then in Jin service; the emperor appointed him prefect of Qi.

sentences.zh: 思溫密令延照言虜情終變，請以幽州內附；

translations.literal: Siwen secretly ordered Yanzhao to say that the barbarians' sentiment would ultimately change, requesting that Youzhou be brought within to submit;
translations.idiomatic: Siwen secretly told Yanzhao that the Khitan mood would eventually shift and urged him to ask that Youzhou be incorporated into Jin;

sentences.zh: 帝不許。

translations.literal: The emperor did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 契丹遣使詣唐，宋齊丘勸唐主厚賄之，俟至淮北，潛遣人殺之，欲以間晉。

translations.literal: The Khitan sent envoys to Tang; Song Qiqiu urged the Tang ruler to bribe them heavily, and when they reached north of the Huai River, secretly dispatch men to kill them, wishing thereby to estrange Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Khitan envoys visited Tang. Song Qiqiu urged the Tang emperor to lavish gifts on them, then secretly have them killed once they crossed north of the Huai, hoping to drive a wedge between Khitan and Jin.

sentences.zh: 壬午，楊光遠奏前澶州刺史馮暉自廣晉城中出戰，因來降，言范延光食盡窮困；

translations.literal: On renwu, Yang Guangyuan memorialized that former Chan Prefecture prefect Feng Hui came out to battle from Guangjin city and therefore came to surrender, stating that Fan Yanguang's food was exhausted and he was destitute and trapped;
translations.idiomatic: On renwu, Yang Guangyuan reported that Feng Hui, former prefect of Chan, had sortied from Guangjin and surrendered, reporting that Fan Yanguang's provisions were exhausted and his plight desperate;

sentences.zh: 己丑，以暉為義成節度使。

translations.literal: On jichou, Hui was made Yicheng military governor.
translations.idiomatic: On jichou, Feng Hui was appointed military governor of Yicheng.

sentences.zh: 楊光遠攻廣晉，歲餘不下，帝以師老民疲，遣內職朱憲入城諭范延光，許移大籓，曰：「若降而殺汝，白日在上，吾無以享國。」

translations.literal: Yang Guangyuan besieged Guangjin for more than a year without taking it; the emperor, because the army was weary and the people exhausted, sent inner service officer Zhu Xian into the city to persuade Fan Yanguang, promising transfer to a great frontier post, saying: "If you surrender and I kill you, with the bright sun above, I would have no means to enjoy the state."
translations.idiomatic: Yang Guangyuan had besieged Guangjin for over a year without success. Concerned that the campaign was exhausting troops and people alike, the emperor sent palace officer Zhu Xian into the city to offer Fan Yanguang a transfer to a major frontier post, swearing: "If I kill you after you surrender, may the sun above witness that I am unfit to rule."

sentences.zh: 延光謂節度副使李式曰：「主上重信，雲不死則不死矣。」

translations.literal: Fan Yanguang said to military deputy commissioner Li Shi: "The sovereign values trust—he says if I am not killed then I will not be killed."
translations.idiomatic: Fan Yanguang told his deputy Li Shi: "The emperor is a man of his word. If he says I won't die, I won't die."

sentences.zh: 乃撤守備，然猶遷延未決。

translations.literal: He then removed defensive preparations, yet still delayed without deciding.
translations.idiomatic: He began dismantling the defenses but still hesitated.

sentences.zh: 宣徽南院使劉處讓復入諭之，延光意乃決。

translations.literal: Xuanhui Southern Court commissioner Liu Churang again entered to persuade him; Yanguang's intent was then decided.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Churang, commissioner of the Southern Xuanhui Court, entered the city again to press the case, and Fan Yanguang finally made up his mind.

sentences.zh: 九月，乙巳朔，楊光遠送延光二子守圖、守英詣大梁。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on the first day of the month yisi, Yang Guangyuan sent Yanguang's two sons Shoutu and Shouying to Daliang.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the ninth month, yisi, Yang Guangyuan sent Fan Yanguang's sons Shoutu and Shouying to Daliang as hostages.

sentences.zh: 己酉，延光遣牙將奉表待罪。

translations.literal: On jiyou, Yanguang sent a staff general to submit a memorial awaiting punishment.
translations.idiomatic: On jiyou, Fan Yanguang sent a staff officer to submit a confession.

sentences.zh: 壬子，詔書至廣晉，延光帥其眾素服於牙門，使者宣詔釋之，朱憲，汴州人也。

translations.literal: On renzi, the edict arrived at Guangjin; Yanguang led his multitude in plain white dress at the headquarters gate; the envoy proclaimed the edict pardoning him. Zhu Xian was a native of Bian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On renzi the pardon arrived at Guangjin. Fan Yanguang led his troops out in white mourning dress to the headquarters gate, where the envoy read the decree of clemency. Zhu Xian was a native of Bianzhou.

sentences.zh: 契丹遣使如洛陽，取趙延壽妻唐燕國長公主以歸。

translations.literal: The Khitan sent envoys to Luoyang to fetch Zhao Yanshou's wife, Tang Princess of Yan State, and return.
translations.idiomatic: Khitan envoys went to Luoyang to escort Zhao Yanshou's wife, the Tang Princess of Yan, back to the steppe.

sentences.zh: 壬戌，唐太府卿趙可封請唐主複姓李，立唐宗廟。

translations.literal: On renxu, Tang Grand Treasury Director Zhao Kefeng requested the Tang ruler restore the surname Li and establish the Tang ancestral temple.
translations.idiomatic: On renxu, Zhao Kefeng, director of the Tang Grand Treasury, urged the Tang emperor to restore the Li surname and erect a Tang ancestral temple.

sentences.zh: 庚午，楊光遠表乞入朝；

translations.literal: On gengwu, Yang Guangyuan submitted a memorial requesting to enter court;
translations.idiomatic: On gengwu, Yang Guangyuan asked permission to come to court;

sentences.zh: 命劉處讓權知天雄軍府事。

translations.literal: Liu Churang was ordered to act as administrator of Tianxiong army headquarters affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Churang was appointed acting administrator of the Tianxiong headquarters.

sentences.zh: 己巳，制以范延光為天平節度使，仍賜鐵券，應廣晉城中將吏軍民今日以前罪皆釋不問；

translations.literal: On jisi, an edict made Fan Yanguang Tianping military governor, still bestowing an iron certificate; for all officers, clerks, soldiers, and civilians within Guangjin city, crimes before today were all pardoned and not questioned;
translations.idiomatic: On jisi an edict appointed Fan Yanguang military governor of Tianping and granted him an iron certificate of immunity. All officers, officials, soldiers, and civilians of Guangjin were pardoned for crimes committed before that day;

sentences.zh: 其張從賓、符彥饒餘黨及自官軍逃叛入城者，亦釋之。

translations.literal: Those who were remnant followers of Zhang Congbin and Fu Yanrao, and those who fled and rebelled from official armies and entered the city, were also pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: including remnant followers of Zhang Congbin and Fu Yanrao and soldiers who had deserted into the city.

sentences.zh: 延光腹心將佐李式、孫漢威、薛霸皆除防禦、團練使、刺史，牙兵皆升為侍衛親軍。

translations.literal: Yanguang's trusted generals and aides Li Shi, Sun Hanwei, and Xue Ba were all made defense commissioners, regiment-training commissioners, and prefects; headquarters soldiers were all promoted to palace guard personal troops.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Yanguang's trusted lieutenants Li Shi, Sun Hanwei, and Xue Ba were made defense commissioners, regiment-training commissioners, and prefects, and his personal troops were enrolled in the imperial guard.

sentences.zh: 初，河陽行軍司馬李彥珣，邢州人也，父母在鄉里，未嘗供饋。

translations.literal: At the beginning, Heyang campaign deputy Li Yanxun, a native of Xing Prefecture, had parents in the hometown and had never supplied them provisions.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yanxun of Xingzhou, deputy military governor of Heyang, had never once sent supplies to his parents back home.

sentences.zh: 後與張從賓同反，從賓敗，奔廣晉，范延光以為步軍都監，使登城拒守。

translations.literal: Later he rebelled together with Zhang Congbin; when Congbin was defeated, he fled to Guangjin; Fan Yanguang made him infantry director and had him mount the walls to resist and defend.
translations.idiomatic: He later joined Zhang Congbin's rebellion. When Zhang was defeated, he fled to Guangjin, where Fan Yanguang made him infantry commander and put him on the walls.

sentences.zh: 楊光遠訪獲其母，置城下以招之，彥王旬引弓射殺其母。

translations.literal: Yang Guangyuan traced and obtained his mother, placed her below the city to summon him; Yanxun drew his bow and shot, killing his mother.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Guangyuan found his mother and placed her below the walls to lure him out. Li Yanxun strung his bow and shot her dead.

sentences.zh: 延光既降，帝以彥珣為坊州刺史。

translations.literal: After Yanguang had surrendered, the emperor made Yanxun prefect of Fang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: After Fan Yanguang surrendered, the emperor appointed Li Yanxun prefect of Fang.

sentences.zh: 近臣言彥珣殺母，殺母惡逆不可赦；

translations.literal: A close minister said Yanxun killed his mother—killing one's mother is abominable rebellion and cannot be pardoned;
translations.idiomatic: A courtier protested that Li Yanxun had murdered his mother—a crime of ultimate treachery that could not be forgiven;

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「赦令已行，不可改也。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "The amnesty edict has already been promulgated—it cannot be changed."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied: "The amnesty has already been issued and cannot be revoked."

sentences.zh: 乃遣之官。

translations.literal: He then sent him to his office.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yanxun was sent to take up his post.

sentences.zh: 臣光曰：治國家者固不可無信。

translations.literal: Your subject Guang says: One who governs a state indeed cannot be without trust.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Guang comments: No ruler can govern without keeping faith.

sentences.zh: 然彥珣之惡，三靈所不容，晉高祖赦其叛君之愆，治其殺母之罪，何損於信哉！

translations.literal: Yet Yanxun's wickedness is what the three spirits cannot tolerate; if Gaozu of Jin pardoned his crime of rebelling against his lord while punished his crime of killing his mother, what harm to trust would there be!
translations.idiomatic: Yet Li Yanxun's crime was one heaven, earth, and the spirits alike could not abide. Had Gaozu of Later Jin forgiven his rebellion but punished his matricide, what would trust have lost?

sentences.zh: 辛未，以楊光遠為天雄節度使。

translations.literal: On xinwei, Yang Guangyuan was made Tianxiong military governor.
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei, Yang Guangyuan was appointed military governor of Tianxiong.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，戊寅，契丹遣使奉寶冊，加帝尊號曰英武明義皇帝。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on wuyin, the Khitan sent envoys bearing seal and document, adding to the emperor the honorific title Heroic Martial Bright Righteous Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter, on wuyin, Khitan envoys arrived bearing seals and documents, investing the emperor with the title Heroic Martial Bright Righteous Emperor.

sentences.zh: 帝以大梁舟車所會，便於漕運，丙辰，建東京於汴州，復以汴州為開封府，以東都為西京，以西都為晉昌軍節度。

translations.literal: The emperor, because Daliang was where boats and carts converged and convenient for grain transport, on bingchen established the Eastern Capital at Bian Prefecture, again made Bian Prefecture Kaifeng Prefecture, made the Eastern Capital the Western Capital, and made the Western Capital Jinchang Army military governorship.
translations.idiomatic: Because Daliang sat at the hub of river and road traffic and was ideal for grain shipment, the emperor on bingchen made Bianzhou the Eastern Capital, restored Kaifeng Prefecture, demoted Luoyang to Western Capital, and reorganized the old western capital as the Jinchang military governorship.

sentences.zh: 帝遣兵部尚書王權使契丹謝尊號，權自以累世將相，恥之，謂人曰：「吾老矣，安能向穹廬屈膝！」

translations.literal: The emperor sent Minister of War Wang Quan as envoy to Khitan to thank them for the honorific title; Quan, considering himself from generations of generals and chancellors, was ashamed, and said to people: "I am old—how can I bow my knees toward the domed tent!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Wang Quan, minister of war, to Khitan to acknowledge the new title. A scion of generations of generals and chancellors, Wang Quan was mortified. He said to others: "I am an old man—how can I kneel before a nomad tent!"

sentences.zh: 乃辭以老疾。

translations.literal: He then declined on grounds of old age and illness.
translations.idiomatic: He pleaded old age and illness to refuse the mission.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，戊子，權坐停官。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry; on wuzi, Quan was punished by dismissal from office.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious. On wuzi, Wang Quan was stripped of his post.

sentences.zh: 初，郭崇韜既死，宰相罕有兼樞密使者。

translations.literal: At the beginning, after Guo Chongtao had died, chancellors rarely concurrently held the post of commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: After Guo Chongtao's death, few chancellors had also served as commissioner of military affairs.

sentences.zh: 帝即位，桑維翰、李崧兼之，宣徽使劉處讓及宦官皆不悅。

translations.literal: When the emperor acceded, Sang Weihan and Li Song concurrently held it; Xuanhui commissioner Liu Churang and eunuchs were all displeased.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor took the throne, Sang Weihan and Li Song held both posts; Liu Churang as Xuanhui commissioner and the eunuchs were displeased.

sentences.zh: 楊光遠圍廣晉，處讓數以軍事銜命往來，光遠奏請多逾分，帝常依違，維翰獨以法裁折之。

translations.literal: Yang Guangyuan besieged Guangjin; Churang repeatedly on military orders went back and forth; Guangyuan's memorial requests often exceeded bounds; the emperor often wavered; Weihan alone used law to judge and restrain him.
translations.idiomatic: During Yang Guangyuan's siege of Guangjin, Liu Churang shuttled back and forth on military business. Yang's demands often overstepped protocol; the emperor usually wavered, but Sang Weihan alone held him to the law.

sentences.zh: 光遠對處讓有不平語，處讓曰：「是皆執政之意。」

translations.literal: Guangyuan had words of discontent toward Churang; Churang said: "These are all the intent of those who hold power."
translations.idiomatic: Yang complained to Liu Churang, who replied: "That is the policy of the chief ministers."

sentences.zh: 光遠由是怨執政。

translations.literal: From this Guangyuan resented those who held power.
translations.idiomatic: From then on Yang Guangyuan nursed a grudge against the chief ministers.

sentences.zh: 范延光降，光遠密表論執政過失；

translations.literal: When Fan Yanguang surrendered, Guangyuan secretly memorialized discussing the faults of those in power;
translations.idiomatic: When Fan Yanguang surrendered, Yang Guangyuan secretly memorialized against the chief ministers;

sentences.zh: 帝知其故而不得已，加維翰兵部尚書，崧工部尚書，皆罷其樞密使；

translations.literal: The emperor knew the reason and had no choice; Weihan was added as Minister of War, Song as Minister of Works—both were removed from commissioner of military affairs;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor understood why and felt he had no choice: Sang Weihan was promoted to minister of war and Li Song to minister of works, and both were stripped of their military commissions;

sentences.zh: 以處讓為樞密使。

translations.literal: Churang was made commissioner of military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Churang was made commissioner of military affairs.

sentences.zh: 太常奏：「今建東京，而宗廟、社稷皆在西京，請遷置大梁。」

translations.literal: The Court of Imperial Sacrifices memorialized: "Now that the Eastern Capital is established, yet the ancestral temple and altars of soil and grain are all in the Western Capital, please move and place them at Daliang."
translations.idiomatic: The Court of Imperial Sacrifices reported: "With the Eastern Capital now established, the ancestral temple and spirit tablets remain in the Western Capital. We ask that they be moved to Daliang."

sentences.zh: 敕旨：「且仍舊。」

translations.literal: Imperial order: "For now, maintain the former arrangement."
translations.idiomatic: The reply came: "For now, leave them where they are."

sentences.zh: 戊戌，大赦。

translations.literal: On wuxu, a general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: On wuxu, a general amnesty was proclaimed.

sentences.zh: 楊延藝故將吳權自愛州舉兵攻皎公羨於交州，公羨遣使以賂求救於漢。

translations.literal: Wu Quan, a former general of Yang Yanyi, raised troops from Ai Prefecture to attack Jiao Gongxian at Jiao Prefecture; Gongxian sent envoys with bribes seeking rescue from Han.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Quan, a former officer of Yang Yanyi, raised troops in Ai Prefecture and attacked Jiao Gongxian in Jiao Prefecture. Gongxian sent envoys with gifts begging aid from Southern Han.

sentences.zh: 漢主欲乘其亂而取之，以其子萬王弘操為靜海節度使，徙封交王，將兵救公羨，漢主自將屯於海門，為之聲援。

translations.literal: The Han ruler wished to take advantage of the chaos to seize it; he made his son Prince Wan Hongcao Jinghai military governor, transferred enfeoffment as Prince of Jiao, led troops to rescue Gongxian; the Han ruler personally commanded encamped at Haimen as sound support for him.
translations.idiomatic: The Han emperor sought to exploit the turmoil and seize the region. He appointed his son Hongcao, Prince of Wan, military governor of Jinghai, created him Prince of Jiao, and sent him to rescue Gongxian, while the emperor himself encamped at Haimen in support.

sentences.zh: 漢主問策於崇文使蕭益，益曰：「今霖雨積旬，海道險遠，吳權桀黠，未可輕也。

translations.literal: The Han ruler asked strategy of Chongwen commissioner Xiao Yi; Yi said: "Now torrential rain has accumulated for ten days; the sea route is perilous and far; Wu Quan is fierce and cunning—it cannot be taken lightly.
translations.idiomatic: The Han emperor consulted Xiao Yi, commissioner of Chongwen. Xiao Yi warned: "Rain has fallen for weeks; the sea route is long and dangerous; Wu Quan is fierce and cunning—not a foe to underestimate.

sentences.zh: 大軍當持重，多用鄉導，然後可進。」

translations.literal: The great army should be steady and weighty, use many local guides extensively, and only then can advance."
translations.idiomatic: The army should advance cautiously with ample local guides—only then should it move."

sentences.zh: 不聽。

translations.literal: He did not listen.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor would not listen.

sentences.zh: 命弘操帥戰艦自白籐江趣交州。

translations.literal: He ordered Hongcao to command war ships from the Baiteng River toward Jiao Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Hongcao to sail his fleet from the Baiteng River toward Jiao Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 權已殺公羨，據交州，引兵逆戰，先於海口多植大杙，銳其首，冒之以鐵，遣輕舟乘潮挑戰而偽遁，弘操逐之，須臾潮落，漢艦皆礙鐵杙不得返，漢兵大敗，士卒覆溺者太半；

translations.literal: Quan had already killed Gongxian and occupied Jiao Prefecture; he led troops to meet in battle; first at the estuary he planted many large stakes, sharpened their heads, capped them with iron; he sent light boats riding the tide to challenge and feign retreat; Hongcao pursued them; in a moment the tide fell; Han ships all struck the iron stakes and could not return; Han troops were greatly defeated; soldiers capsized and drowned—more than half;
translations.idiomatic: Wu Quan had already killed Gongxian and held Jiao Prefecture. He marched out to meet the invaders after driving iron-tipped stakes into the estuary. He sent light boats down the tide to skirmish and pretend to flee. Hongcao gave chase; when the tide suddenly ebbed, the Han ships ran onto the stakes and could not escape. The Han army was routed; more than half the men drowned.

sentences.zh: 弘操死，漢主慟哭，收餘眾而還。

translations.literal: Hongcao died; the Han ruler wailed in grief, gathered the remaining multitude and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Hongcao was killed. The Han emperor mourned bitterly and withdrew with the survivors.

sentences.zh: 先是，著作佐郎侯融勸漢主弭兵息民，至是以兵不振，追咎融，剖棺暴其屍。

translations.literal: Before this, editorial assistant Hou Rong had urged the Han ruler to cease arms and rest the people; now because the army did not prosper, he pursued blame on Rong, opened the coffin and exposed his corpse.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, editorial assistant Hou Rong had urged the Han emperor to end warfare and ease the people's burdens. Now, blaming him for the defeat, the emperor had his coffin opened and his corpse displayed.

sentences.zh: 益，仿之孫也。

translations.literal: Yi was the grandson of Fang.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Yi was a grandson of Xiao Fang.

sentences.zh: 楚順賢夫人彭氏卒。

translations.literal: Chu Consort Shunxian Lady Peng died.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Peng, Consort Shunxian of Chu, died.

sentences.zh: 彭夫人貌陋而治家有法，楚王希範憚之；

translations.literal: Lady Peng's appearance was homely yet she governed the household with method; Chu king Xifan feared her;
translations.idiomatic: Plain in appearance but meticulous in running the household, Lady Peng kept King Xifan of Chu in awe;

sentences.zh: 既卒，希範始縱聲色，為長夜之飲，內外無別。

translations.literal: After she died, Xifan began to indulge in music and women, making all-night drinking; inner and outer were undifferentiated.
translations.idiomatic: After her death Xifan gave himself over to pleasure, hosting nights of endless revelry and ignoring all distinction between private and public life.

sentences.zh: 有商人妻美，希範殺其夫而奪之，妻誓不辱，自經死。

translations.literal: There was a merchant's wife who was beautiful; Xifan killed her husband and seized her; the wife vowed not to be shamed and hanged herself to death.
translations.idiomatic: When he saw a merchant's beautiful wife, Xifan killed her husband and took her. She chose death by hanging rather than submit.

sentences.zh: 河決鄆州。

translations.literal: The Yellow River burst its banks at Yan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The Yellow River breached its banks at Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 十一月，范延光自鄆州入朝。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, Fan Yanguang from Yan Prefecture entered court.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, Fan Yanguang came to court from Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 丙午，以閩主昶為閩國王，以左散騎常侍盧損為冊禮使，賜昶赭袍。

translations.literal: On bingwu, the Min ruler Chang was made King of Min; Left Regular Cavalry Attendant Lu Sun was made investiture envoy; Chang was bestowed an ochre robe.
translations.idiomatic: On bingwu, the Min ruler Chang was created King of Min; Lu Sun, Left Regular Cavalry Attendant, was sent as investiture envoy, and Chang was granted an ochre robe.

sentences.zh: 戊申，以威武節度使王繼恭為臨海郡王。

translations.literal: On wushen, Weiwu military governor Wang Jigong was made Prince of Linhai.
translations.idiomatic: On wushen, Wang Jigong, military governor of Weiwu, was created Prince of Linhai.

sentences.zh: 閩主聞之，遣進奏官林恩白執政，以既襲帝號，辭冊命及使者。

translations.literal: When the Min ruler heard this, he sent memorial-presenting officer Lin En to inform those in power that, having already assumed an imperial title, he declined the investiture mandate and envoy.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing this, the Min ruler sent memorial officer Lin En to inform the court that, having already taken an imperial title, he declined the investiture and the envoy.

sentences.zh: 閩諫議大夫黃諷以閩主淫暴，與妻子辭訣入諫，閩主欲杖之，諷曰：「臣若迷國不忠，死亦無怨；

translations.literal: Min Remonstrance Counsellor Huang Feng, because the Min ruler was licentious and tyrannical, took leave of his wife and children and entered to remonstrate; the Min ruler wished to beat him with sticks; Feng said: "If your servant were deluded to the state and disloyal, even death would be without resentment;
translations.idiomatic: Huang Feng, remonstrance counsellor of Min, believing the ruler debauched and cruel, bade farewell to his wife and children and went to remonstrate. When the Min ruler moved to have him beaten, Huang Feng said: "If I have misled the state and been disloyal, I deserve death without complaint;

sentences.zh: 直諫被杖，臣不受也。」

translations.literal: For straight remonstrance to be beaten with sticks—your servant will not accept it."
translations.idiomatic: but to be beaten for speaking plainly—that I will not accept."

sentences.zh: 閩主怒，黜為民。

translations.literal: The Min ruler was angry and demoted him to commoner status.
translations.idiomatic: The Min ruler in fury reduced him to commoner status.

sentences.zh: 帝患天雄節度使楊光遠跋扈難制，桑維翰請分天雄之眾，加光遠太尉、西京留守兼河陽節度使。

translations.literal: The emperor was troubled that Tianxiong military governor Yang Guangyuan was overbearing and hard to control; Sang Weihan requested dividing Tianxiong's forces, adding to Guangyuan Grand Marshal, Western Capital garrison commander concurrently Heyang military governor.
translations.idiomatic: Alarmed that Yang Guangyuan, military governor of Tianxiong, had grown too powerful to control, Sang Weihan proposed splitting his army and promoting him to grand marshal while making him garrison commander of the Western Capital and military governor of Heyang.

sentences.zh: 光遠由是怨望，密以賂自訴於契丹，養部曲千餘人，常蓄異志。

translations.literal: Guangyuan from this nursed resentment, secretly with bribes made self-appeal to Khitan, kept over a thousand personal troops, and often harbored different intent.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Guangyuan resentfully sent secret gifts to the Khitan court to plead his case, kept more than a thousand retainers, and nursed designs of rebellion.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，建鄴都於廣晉府，置彰德軍於相州，以澶、衛隸之；

translations.literal: On xinhai, Yecheng Capital was established at Guangjin prefecture headquarters; Zhangde Army was placed at Xiang Prefecture, with Chan and Wei subordinate to it;
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai, the Yecheng capital was established at Guangjin; the Zhangde army was stationed at Xiangzhou with Chan and Wei placed under its command;

sentences.zh: 置永清軍於貝州，以博、冀隸之。

translations.literal: Yongqing Army was placed at Bei Prefecture, with Bo and Ji subordinate to it.
translations.idiomatic: the Yongqing army was stationed at Beizhou with Bo and Ji placed under its command.

sentences.zh: 澶州舊治頓丘，帝慮契丹為後世之患，遣前淄州刺史汲人劉繼勳徙澶州跨德勝津，並頓丘徙焉。

translations.literal: Chanzou had formerly been administered from Dunqiu; fearing the Khitan as a menace to later ages, the emperor sent Liu Jixun of Ji, former prefect of Zi, to move Chanzou across the Desheng Ford and to relocate Dunqiu there as well.
translations.idiomatic: Chanzou had long been administered from Dunqiu. Fearing the Khitan as a threat to future generations, the emperor sent Liu Jixun of Ji, former prefect of Zi, to move Chanzou across the Desheng Ford and relocate Dunqiu there with it.

sentences.zh: 以河南尹高行周為廣晉尹、鄴都留守，貝州防禦使王廷胤為彰德節度使，右神武統軍王周為永清節度使。

translations.literal: Henan governor Gao Xingzhou was made Guangjin governor and Yecheng garrison commander; Wang Tingyin, defense commissioner of Beizhou, was made military governor of Zhangde; Wang Zhou, commander of the Right Divine Martial Army, was made military governor of Yongqing.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Xingzhou, governor of Henan, was appointed Guangjin governor and Yecheng garrison commander; Wang Tingyin, defense commissioner of Beizhou, became military governor of Zhangde; and Wang Zhou, commander of the Right Divine Martial Army, became military governor of Yongqing.

sentences.zh: 廷胤，處存之孫；

translations.literal: Tingyin was a grandson of Wang Chucun;
translations.idiomatic: Tingyin was a grandson of Wang Chucun;

sentences.zh: 周，鄴都人也。

translations.literal: Zhou was a native of Yecheng.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou came from Yecheng.

sentences.zh: 范延光屢請致仕，甲寅，詔以太子太師致仕，居於大梁，每預宴會，與群臣無異。

translations.literal: Fan Yanguang repeatedly requested retirement; on jiayin, an edict granted him retirement as Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent; he dwelt at Daliang and attended every banquet no differently from the other ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Yanguang repeatedly asked to retire. On jiayin, the court granted him retirement as Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent. He lived at Daliang and attended every banquet on equal footing with the other ministers.

sentences.zh: 延光之反也，相州刺史掖人王景拒境不從，戊午，以景為耀州團練使。

translations.literal: When Yanguang rebelled, Wang Jing of Ye, prefect of Xiangzhou, held his borders and would not follow him; on wuwu, Jing was made training commissioner of Yao Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: During Yanguang's rebellion, Wang Jing of Ye, prefect of Xiangzhou, held his borders and refused to join him. On wuwu, Jing was appointed training commissioner of Yao Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 癸亥，敕聽公私自鑄銅錢，無得雜以鉛鐵，每十錢重一兩，以「天福無寶」為文。

translations.literal: On guihai, an edict permitted the public and private parties to cast copper cash, forbidding admixture of lead or iron; every ten coins were to weigh one liang, inscribed with the legend "Tianfu Without Treasure."
translations.idiomatic: On guihai, an edict allowed public and private casting of copper cash, with no lead or iron mixed in. Every ten coins were to weigh one liang and bear the inscription "Tianfu Without Treasure."

sentences.zh: 仍令鹽鐵頒下模範，惟禁私作銅器。

translations.literal: The Salt and Iron Commission was also ordered to distribute casting molds, while private manufacture of copper vessels alone was forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: The Salt and Iron Commission was to distribute official molds, while only private manufacture of copper vessels remained forbidden.

sentences.zh: 立右金吾衛上將軍重貴為鄭王，充開封尹。

translations.literal: The Right Golden Crow Guard senior general Chonggui was installed as Prince of Zheng and appointed metropolitan governor of Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: Right Golden Crow Guard senior general Chonggui was installed as Prince of Zheng and appointed metropolitan governor of Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 庚辰，敕先許公私鑄錢，慮銅難得，聽輕重從便，但勿令缺漏。

translations.literal: On gengchen, an edict noted that since public and private coinage had already been permitted, yet copper was hard to obtain, weight might vary at convenience so long as the coins were not defective or incomplete.
translations.idiomatic: On gengchen, the court noted that because copper was scarce despite permission for public and private coinage, weight might vary as needed so long as the coins were sound and complete.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，吳讓皇卒。

translations.literal: On xinchou, the Abdicated Emperor of Wu died.
translations.idiomatic: On xinchou, Wu's Abdicated Emperor died.

sentences.zh: 唐王廢朝二十七日，追謚曰睿皇帝。

translations.literal: The Tang king suspended court for twenty-seven days and posthumously honored him as Emperor Rui.
translations.idiomatic: The Tang king suspended court for twenty-seven days and posthumously honored him as Emperor Rui.

sentences.zh: 是歲，唐主徙吳王璟為齊王。

translations.literal: That year, the Tang ruler transferred Prince of Wu Jing to be Prince of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: That year, the Tang ruler transferred Prince of Wu Jing to the title of Prince of Qi.

sentences.zh: 鳳翔節度使李從曮，厚文士而薄武人，愛農民而嚴士卒，由是將士怨之。

translations.literal: Li Congyan, military governor of Fengxiang, favored literati and slighted warriors, cherished farmers yet was harsh toward soldiers, and for this the officers and men resented him.
translations.idiomatic: Li Congyan, military governor of Fengxiang, favored scholars over soldiers and peasants over troops, and for that the army came to resent him.

sentences.zh: 會發兵戌西邊，既出郊，作亂，突門入城，剽掠於市。

translations.literal: When troops were mobilized to garrison the western frontier, they had barely left the suburbs when they mutinied, burst through the gates into the city, and plundered the markets.
translations.idiomatic: When troops were sent to garrison the western frontier, they had barely left the suburbs before they mutinied, stormed the gates, and looted the markets.

sentences.zh: 從曮發帳下兵擊之，亂兵帳，東走，欲自訴於朝廷，至華州，鎮國節度使太原張彥澤邀擊，盡誅之。

translations.literal: Congyan sent his personal guard to strike them; the mutineers broke camp and fled east, intending to appeal to the court themselves; reaching Huazhou, Zhang Yanzhe of Taiyuan, military governor of Zhenguo, intercepted and killed them all.
translations.idiomatic: Congyan sent his personal guard against them. The mutineers broke camp and fled east, hoping to plead their case before the court. At Huazhou, Zhang Yanzhe of Taiyuan, military governor of Zhenguo, intercepted them and slaughtered them to the last man.
